## ⛔ D76 · RAILWAY WEBHOOKS — deploy visibility and a volume alert — 2026-10-09

✅ Owner 10-09, after Railway's changelog (*custom headers for project webhooks*). **Why:** **Resume Master's `merge: A82 + A83 + …` deployment shows FAILED in the dashboard and nobody was told**; **O65** (*a push is not a deploy*) was found by accident; and **draft's volume reached 481 / 500 MB once.** Railway project webhooks push **deployment status changes and alert events** (a deployment failed or crashed, an out-of-memory kill, a volume alert, a monitor trigger) to **any URL**, configured **per project across all environments** — so one webhook covers `draft` **and** `resume-master`.

◐ **SET UP 10-07 (38g, late), on the owner's go:** `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` generated locally (36 random bytes, kept in `draft-secrets/RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.txt` under the owner's home folder, outside the repo; set on draft through the CLI's stdin; never printed) · **the project webhook created** (`ec579f62`) → `https://jobsviadraft.com/api/hooks/railway`, events failed · crashed · oom_killed · deployed · removed · VolumeAlert triggered / resolved · Monitor triggered / resolved, production only. ⛔ **Its `Authorization` header is NOT set:** the Railway tool takes no headers and the API refused the CLI's token for `notificationRuleUpdate` ("Not Authorized") — **the owner adds it in the dashboard** (Project Settings → Webhooks → the hook → Custom headers → `Authorization` = `Bearer ` + the file's contents); until then deliveries get 401 (harmless). ⭐ **Found while setting it up:** Railway's event NAMES (`deployed`, `redeployed`, `oom_killed`, `restarted`, `resumed`, `slept`) are not deployment statuses and the parser dropped them — fixed; `oom_killed` is an alarm. Was: ✅ **STEP 2 BUILT 10-07 (38g) ahead of Step 1, local, NOT pushed — migration 143.** Built first because the two unknowns were answerable from Railway's own docs (read through the Railway docs tool, `observability/webhooks`): ✅ **custom headers are real** (up to 20 per webhook, values write-only, sent with every delivery and with *Test Webhook*), and ⛔ **payloads are NOT signed** — the header IS the authentication. The payload is `{ type: "Deployment.<state>", details: { id, commitHash, commitAuthor, commitMessage, … }, resource: { workspace, project, environment, service, deployment }, severity, timestamp }`; delivery retries 3× and counts any 2xx/3xx as success. ⚠ **The volume- and monitor-alert type strings are NOT published** — accepted by family prefix (`Volume…`, `Monitor…`, `Alert…`); any other type is dropped with its NAME logged, so **the owner's *Test Webhook* reveals what Railway actually sends**.
- `POST /api/hooks/railway` (`routes/railwayHook.js`, mounted before the global parser): **`Authorization: Bearer <RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN>`**, constant-time; anything else **401 with no body** (no token on the server = the same 401: off, not open) · its own **16 KB** cap (413) · **60 / minute** per address (429) · `shared/deployEvents.js` keeps **the type, family, state, severity, project / environment / service names, service + deployment ids and the commit hash — never the commit message or author** (a person), malformed ids dropped · ⛔ read-only: one INSERT into `deploy_events`, an empty **204** whether kept or dropped, nothing echoed.
- **Admin → Ops → "Deployments"**: the last event per service — **red** for `failed` / `crashed` and for any volume / monitor alert (one rule, `isAlarm`) — with **this server's commit and latest applied migration** beside it, so a push that did not deploy shows.
- **Tests** `test/d76RailwayHook.test.js` (7): no / wrong header → 401, no body · unknown types dropped, same empty 204 · oversize 413, non-JSON 400 · **no table but `deploy_events` changes** · ids only · the rate limit · `Deployment.failed` → red, read through the shared rule — ⭐ four mutations (auth, the type rule, the cap, the alarm rule), each red. `npm test` **3813 / 3813 / 0**.
- **For the owner's Step 1, add to the webhook:** URL `https://jobsviadraft.com/api/hooks/railway` · a custom header `Authorization` = `Bearer <a long random value>` · the same value as `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` on the draft service (batch it with the other pending variable changes — each restarts production) · press **Test Webhook** and read Admin → Ops (or the log line naming a dropped type). A second webhook to Discord / Slack for the human alert is unaffected.

**STEP 1 · THE OWNER — five minutes, no code:**
- A **Discord or Slack webhook** (Railway has built-in support for both) subscribed to **`Deployment.failed`**, **crashed**, **OOM killed**.
- A **volume alert on `draft-data` at ~80%** (and `resume-master-data`). ⚠ *Confirm the exact event names in the Webhooks tab — they are chosen from a list there.*
- **Check the service's `Backups` tab:** are **Railway's volume backups enabled for `draft-data`**, on what schedule, and has **one ever been restored into a scratch volume?** Draft's own daily backups live **on the same volume** as the database.

**STEP 2 · THE AGENT — small, after Step 1:** `POST /api/hooks/railway` — **a public endpoint, so it is hostile-input code:**
- ⛔ **Authenticate with a custom header** (`Authorization: Bearer …`, secret `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`), **constant-time compare**, refuse everything else with 401 and **no body.** ⚠ Confirm in the Webhooks tab that the header can be set — the owner reports the feature as shipped.
- **Accept known event types only**; **cap the payload size**; **rate-limit**; ⛔ **read-only — the endpoint logs, it never acts**, and never trusts a field to drive behaviour.
- Store **event type, service, environment, deployment id, commit, time** in `deploy_events` — ⛔ **ids only, no secrets**, nothing from the payload echoed back.

## ⛔ D75 · THE CRAWLER WORKER — a pilot that finds boards and learns where Apply lands — 2026-10-08

✅ Owner 10-08: a VM could prove useful for *the crawl, freshness and adding companies via the ATS domains* — *"explore companies and get back with the URLs."* **"Gated" meant non-ToS public pages, not LinkedIn-class sites.** The owner is **getting the VM / keys**; **build it so it can be wired and tested shortly.** **The design is `docs/CRAWLER_WORKER.md` — read it first.**

1. ⛔ **A VM adds nothing to crawling postings** — the ATS boards are public JSON and the existing adapters stay in charge. **The pilot's two jobs:** **J1 find a company's board** (which ATS and slug — *the volume problem, D74 P3*) and **J2 learn where Apply lands** (D67 part 1, the sweep O84 says needs attended work). **J3 (custom career sites) is out of the pilot.**
2. ⛔ **A worker that cannot reach the database:** it **leases a task** from `GET /api/crawler/next` and **returns a signed result** to `POST /api/crawler/result`. **No DB credentials, no user data, no model call.** Its only secret is `CRAWLER_TOKEN`. **A separate service from the one that will hold user sessions (E3)** — the pilot rehearses that boundary.
3. **Ladder, browser last:** plain HTTP over `/careers` first (`detectKnownAtsMatch` already exists) → **only if empty and client-rendered**, the browser, reading **the network log** (the page's own call to `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>` is the best evidence). **Results go through the existing harvest → `validateBoard` → admin dry-run add. ⛔ Never auto-enabled.**
4. ⛔ **Rules of engagement — the line is ToS and robots, not technique:** **public pages only** · **`robots.txt` honoured** · an **identifying User-Agent** and a public `/crawler` page · **per-host rate limits** · **a fresh context per company** · **never** log in, type, submit, solve a CAPTCHA, evade a challenge or record a query string · **a data-driven, owner-editable DENY-LIST** (`linkedin.com`, `indeed.com`, `glassdoor.com`, `ziprecruiter.com`, `monster.com` …) that wins over every task · a takedown adds a domain the same day.
5. ⛔ **SSRF guard:** task URLs come from untrusted data — refuse `localhost`, private ranges, link-local and the cloud-metadata address, **re-checked after every redirect.**

## ⛔⛔ D118 · THE ATLAS IS LIVE — content added without a rebuild; counts move as postings arrive and leave — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"we should be able to do this such that when we add to base files of the atlas, that should reflect in production rather than having to rebuild it and the counts and metrics dynamic, as in a new job is ingested featuring python, that should reflect across the postings we show."*

**P1 · COUNTS MOVE WITH THE BOARD (no nightly wait):** when a posting is **ingested, updated, closed or expires**, the same transaction that writes it **re-matches its skills once (the one `postingMatcher`) and adjusts the per-node counts** — `atlas_node_stats` gains / loses that posting (total, per role, per level read, per family) — and writes its D114 spans. Every surface reads those live rows: Atlas pages, the hover popup, Your map, role and family maps, the board's skill tags. **The nightly pass stays as the reconciliation** (a full recount; any drift it corrects is logged as a number, which should be 0). Caches: the peek route and page data are invalidated on a count change (or a 60-second cap), never the old 1-hour cache. ⚠ **The boilerplate fix (pending the owner's yes) belongs in the same matcher** — strip text repeated across a company's postings before counting.
**P2 · CONTENT CHANGES WITHOUT A DEPLOY:** the database is the source of the Atlas's content in production; files are an import route, not the source. (a) **Admin → Atlas → Import content**: the owner uploads the tracker HTML (or the extracted JSON); **the extraction runs in the owner's browser** (the same extractor, compiled for the client — the server never evaluates an uploaded script), the JSON goes to the server, which **validates it against the schema**, shows a **diff** (added / changed / removed steps, items, patterns, concepts — by ID) and applies it on **Apply**; progress keyed on IDs survives. (b) The node editor, Find on Wikipedia, Draft definitions and publish / unpublish already act live — confirm none waits for a restart. (c) The boot import of `content/learn/*.json` runs ONLY on an empty table (first install), never over newer database content. **TESTS:** `d118IngestMovesCounts` (a new posting asking for Python → Python's count +1 on the next read, no nightly) · `d118CloseMovesCounts` · `d118NightlyDriftZero` · `d118SpansAtIngest` · `d118CacheInvalidatedOnChange` · `d118ImportValidatesAndDiffs` · `d118ServerNeverEvaluatesUpload` · `d118ImportKeepsProgress` · `d118BootImportOnlyWhenEmpty`.
**✅ P2 DONE 10-31 (43v) — `509634e` + `1cb7fd0`, PUSHED; migration 198 (`learn_content`, `atlas_changes`).** The Learn content is a versioned row in `learn_content`; every reader (`/api/learn`, progress, step links, Your map's Learn next, the boot imports) reads `learnContent(db)`; `/api/learn` cache 1 h → 60 s. (a) Admin → Atlas → Import content (`adminLearnImport.jsx`): the tracker's data block runs in a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe with CSP `default-src 'none'` (no origin, cookies, storage or network) and posts back JSON only; a `.json` file is parsed, never run (shared extractor `shared/learnTracker.js`). `/api/admin/learn` (`requireAdmin`): `GET /content` · `POST /import/preview` (validate field by field, unknown fields refused incl. `__proto__`, ids unique, refs real, links http(s); diff by id; writes nothing) · `POST /import/apply { content, base }` (409 if the content moved since the preview). Apply re-runs the D115 imports; an owner definition still in its old words takes the new words, a typed or accepted one is kept; **progress is never touched** (a mark on a removed id counts again if the id returns). (b) Every curator tool acts live; **one real staleness bug fixed** — the search index and D114's link list were keyed on count + newest second, so publish B / unpublish A in one second left A searchable; now keyed on `atlas_changes` (triggers on `atlas_nodes` and `skill_synonyms`; ⚠ a rebuild of `atlas_nodes` like 194's drops the triggers — recreate them). After a Find on Wikipedia pick, the summary still waits for Refresh Wikipedia / the nightly run (as the panel says). (c) `seedLearnContentIfEmpty` imports `content/learn/*.json` only on an empty table. 6 tests (the 4 named + `d118BrowserExtractsPage`, `d118CuratorToolsLive`); 9 mutations each red. ⚠ The import panel and sandbox were not walked in a real Chrome. **✅ P1 DONE 10-31 (43v) — `fa00545`, PUSHED; migration 199 (`atlas_posting_match`, `atlas_role_level_stats`, `atlas_live_state`, the queue `atlas_posting_dirty`).** `services/atlas/atlasLive.js`: a posting's change is read ONCE by `postingMatcher` (new `read(p)`: counted + linked nodes in one pass) and its old contribution subtracted / new added — node postings, per role, per level, board totals; `atlas_posting_match` stores what each posting added, so a close subtracts exactly that. **Write paths:** triggers on `scraped_jobs` queue every insert / relevant change / delete (any writer, scripts too, is caught on the next read); the crawl upsert + prune, `ingestJob`, live-search write-back, `runExpiredJobsCleanup`, dedup retire / restore, `boardAge.retireRows`, import revert, the manual close, detail fetch, the description backfill, the level read and enrichment import / revert also drain it in their own transaction. Every surface (peek, node page, Your map, role page, D114 terms) drains first. The nightly `computeAtlasStats` is the recount and logs `[Cron] atlas drift: N`. Peek `max-age` 3600 → 60; server-side page / peek data ≤ 60 s and dropped on a counts-version or `atlasChangeCount` change. **Measured on a copy (2,616 forced active, 609 nodes):** ingest + update median 11.3 ms (OpenAI, 565 postings) / 6.8 ms (4 postings), close 9.6 ms; a boilerplate threshold crossing re-reads that company's affected postings (4 of 40 ingests); **drift 0** after the baseline and after 60 writes. 6 tests (5 named + `d118PerIngestCost`), 13 mutations red; the lane 767 / 767 over 83 files; 158 / 158 re-run on `main`; boot smoke `latestApplied 199_atlas_live_counts`. **Not live:** per family (no family field until D116 M1); pay range, "asked with" and board edges stay nightly; a new node / alias is not a posting write — the nightly reports it as drift with `vocabChanged: true`. ⚠ Found, pre-existing: repeating the full pass in one process slows ≈ 1.3 s → 5–10 s by the third run (heap flat; `main`'s matcher shows the same) — harmless once a day, unprofiled.

## ⛔⛔ [STRATEGY] D185 · THE GROWTH PLAN REVIEWED — what to adopt, change or reject from the owner's four-phase plan, and what to build (after the FIRST PRIORITY) — 2026-11-09

✅ Owner 11-09 (pasted a four-phase plan: Phase 1 a dual feed — Hirebase / Fantastic.jobs bulk + Jobo's MCP for the agentic résumé, freshness alerts as the hook; Phase 2 learning as a data flywheel — skill tags, reverse technographics, a reward loop; Phase 3 a path to ATS partnerships — a shadow integration, source tagging, a "Trojan horse", a pitch with the volume; Phase 4 monetisation — technographic lead gen, verified talent pools): *"look at our phased approaches and direction and analyse what we have and what we need … upsides and downsides, what we should put on the worklog to build, which of these to adopt and why or why not, are there better ideas, strategies, alternatives."* **Reviewed by the chat assistant against this log. Not legal advice.**
**THE FRAMING, CORRECTED:** the plan opens on the marketplace chicken-and-egg, but **draft's supply side is not the bottleneck** — A112's crawler holds ≈ 80k postings read from employers' own ATS boards, and D140's feed covers the rest. Job seekers don't need employers to join for the board to work. **The real constraints are (1) DEMAND — getting the right job seekers to show up and come back, and (2) PROOF OF QUALITY — showing that draft's applicants get interviews.** Employers and ATS vendors only matter once (2) exists. So the plan's order is right, and its centre of gravity should move from "volume" to "distribution + outcomes".
**WHAT EXISTS vs THE PLAN (verified in the log):** feed structure ✅ (crawler + D140; TheirStack trial approved 11-08) · learning platform ✅ (Atlas: courses, checks, proof, readiness — D169 / D172 / D178) · skill tags from learning ✅ (*Proven in Atlas* on the profile and résumé — D169 / D183) · technographics ✅ (D179 (5), from postings) · the gap loop ✅ (D177) · public profiles ✅ (D183) · public board + company pages ✅ (D179) · networking ✅ built, OFF until counsel (D180) · extension autofill ✅ (no auto-submit — D36's refusal) · server-side full auto ✅ code, held by the safety gate (D175) · freshness alerts ⬜ (D113's picks email only; no "new match" alert) · outcome tracking ⬜ (needs the Inbox — D112 / D103 — not set up) · employer side ⬜ none.
**VERDICTS, PHASE BY PHASE:**
**P1a · Bulk feed as a baseline — ADOPT, CHANGED.** *Up:* instant coverage of categories and companies the crawler misses. *Down:* licences (D140 P0: **Jobo's terms forbid a competing job-data product** — that collides with the Skills Index and D134's Atlas API; **Fantastic.jobs publishes no licence**; **Hirebase was never evaluated**), duplicates and ghost jobs, cost per useful posting, a dependency that can change terms. *So:* run the **TheirStack trial already approved** through the same pipeline (one dedupe, D127's leak rule, D137's ghost score) and measure cost per useful posting; **Hirebase or Fantastic.jobs only after written answers to D140's four questions** (display · derived data / Skills Index / API · public pages · keeping history); **the crawler stays the primary source** (direct, freshest, free, ours). Filtering to the learning platform's audience = D179's taxonomy + the person's placement (B-1) — already the mechanism.
**P1b · Jobo's MCP for the agentic résumé — REJECT.** *Why:* draft already reads the source ATS's own JSON for Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby (no middleman needed for "clean JSON"); Jobo was retired (never delivered a row) and its no-compete clause conflicts with D134; an MCP hop adds a third party, latency, cost and a privacy surface **inside the apply path, where candidate data flows**. **Better (build D185-1): draft's own application-schema reader** — per ATS, the posting's real application questions from the ATS's public endpoints (e.g. Greenhouse's job board API can return a job's questions), cached per posting and fed to the semi / full-auto fill and to tailoring. Same benefit, no dependency.
**P1c · Freshness alerts as the hook — ADOPT (the best idea in the plan).** *Up:* habit, return visits, "apply in the first hour" is a real edge; cheap — the crawler already runs. *Down:* alert fatigue; freshness claims ("beats LinkedIn") are hard to prove — don't market them until measured. **Build D185-2:** *"A new job that fits your résumé, posted <N> minutes ago"* — only top-tier matches (D184 B-8) that pass the live check and the ghost score; **email now (Resend is live), push later (VAPID)**; a daily digest by default, instant as an opt-in, a hard cap per day; measure time-from-posting-to-alert per source and report it in Admin.
**P2a · Skill tags from learning — ALREADY BUILT; keep the wording.** Call it **"Proven on draft"** (a check or a build, with its date) — **never "verified"** to employers: D183's rule, and an honest claim is what makes it worth anything.
**P2b · Reverse technographics — ADOPT, CHANGED.** *Up:* Atlas teaches what the market is starting to ask for. *Down:* **auto-generated learning paths** are a quality and licensing risk (D176: AI-use terms, no-copy rules; a wrong lesson teaches people wrong things). **Build D185-3:** a *rising skills* signal from D179's technographics (skills whose share of postings is growing, by subcategory) **joined with D177's unanswered asks** → the ranked Atlas content backlog; the agent may **draft** a path outline from open-licensed register items for **human review** — nothing auto-published. Public version = D150's *Your market this week* / Skills Index pages (also SEO).
**P2c · The reward loop — ADOPT, with honesty.** *Up:* closes learn → apply. **Build D185-4:** finishing a check / module shows **"Add <skill> to your résumé"** (truthful, through the claim guard — never invents scope) **+ "5 jobs this unlocks"** — the jobs where that skill moves the person up a tier (B-8), with the match before → after. (D178 already has the résumé half.)
**P3a · Shadow integration (extension / headless) — ALREADY BUILT; keep the guard rails.** The extension fills, the person submits (D36); full auto is server-side behind FA6. Volume through it is earned by quality, not pushed.
**P3b · Source tagging — ADOPT, CHANGED to the ATS's own attribution.** Use each ATS's **documented source parameter on the job's apply link** (the way job boards are credited; the agent verifies each ATS's docs), and answer *"How did you hear about us?"* with *draft* **only when true and the person agreed**. Never hidden text in fields, never anything that misrepresents the candidate. (Unrelated to 10-07's rule that strips `utm_*` from stored evidence URLs — that's about what we keep, not what we send.)
**P3c · The "Trojan horse" and the headless-volume pitch — REJECT the framing.** *Why:* (1) recruiters already treat mass auto-apply tools as spam; **tagging bulk applications with draft's name brands draft as the spam source**, and employers can filter that source out in one click — the tag works against us unless quality is visibly high; (2) ATS vendors and their customers see automation of their forms as abuse (bot checks, terms of use); **pitching an ATS by saying "we already drive thousands of automated applications into your customers' forms" invites a block or a legal letter, not a partnership**; (3) the plan's own Phase 4 depends on employer trust, which this spends. **Better — three moves that get to the same partnership honestly:** **(i) quality as the metric:** caps per person per day, only top-tier matches, honest résumés (claim guard) → measure **interview rate per application** (needs outcome tracking — D185-5) and lead with that number; **(ii) customer pull:** a small employer pilot (5–20 Boston startups on Greenhouse / Ashby / Lever): their company page claimed and corrected (D179), draft's best-matched, opted-in candidates introduced to them free — **ATS vendors build integrations when their customers ask**; **(iii) apply to the ATS partner programmes early** (most publish partner tracks for job boards and sourcing tools) with the pilot's results, not volume.
**P4a · Technographic lead gen for B2B — DEFER.** *Down:* **TheirStack and Jobo terms forbid reselling or building a competing data product from their data**; companies like TheirStack already sell exactly this; for a solo founder it's a second business. *If ever:* only from draft's OWN crawl, company-level only, never people. Use technographics now as **user value** (company pages, Your match) and **content** (market pages → SEO).
**P4b · Talent pools — ADOPT as the long-term business, built on consent.** A reverse marketplace (employers pay to reach or be introduced to opted-in candidates) is the natural end state of D183 + D169. *Rules:* candidates opt in per employer or per pool (*"open to employers"* — a new D183 visibility), "proven on draft" with evidence (never "verified"), **no personal data sold**, counsel first. Start as the concierge pilot in P3c (ii) — learn before building.
**BETTER IDEAS THE PLAN MISSES (recommended):** **(1) A BEACHHEAD NICHE: international students and visa-dependent job seekers** (OPT / STEM OPT / H-1B) — the owner's own situation; high intent, underserved, word-of-mouth dense (university international offices, student groups, forums); draft already has the pieces (H-1B / PERM history on company pages, the sponsorship filter A109, D179's *"at companies that have sponsored H-1B"*). *"Jobs that actually sponsor, ranked to your résumé, within the hour"* is a sharper hook than freshness alone. **(2) SEARCH AS THE MAIN ACQUISITION CHANNEL:** D128 / D179's public pages — **"<role> jobs that sponsor H-1B in <city>"**, company pages with sponsorship history, market pages — programmatic pages with real, live data (expired jobs removed fast; no thin pages — D179's minimum count). **(3) FREE TOOLS AS THE TOP OF THE FUNNEL:** D141's résumé honesty check, an ATS match check, *"Does this company sponsor?"* — shareable, no sign-up for one use. **(4) OUTCOMES AS THE NORTH STAR:** interviews per active user (not applications sent) — this needs the Inbox (D112 Gmail / D103 forwarding), **so the Inbox moves from "when ready" to strategic**. **(5) UNIVERSITY CAREER CENTRES** (Northeastern first) — distribution + a natural first cohort. **(6) THE VIRAL LOOPS ALREADY DESIGNED:** Send a job (public link — D180 / D179), public profiles (D183) — switch Network on when counsel answers.

**▶ 11-09 (later) — OWNER: *"may be hirebase is enough cause they do technographics too … how does the tiers work, is it custom feed or bulk feed, cause if we get a bunch of house keeping leads its useless for us … high quality custom data to feed into our system roles and that too within a set, say 1-3 month timeline would be great and usa only."*** **Read by the chat assistant from Hirebase's pricing page and API docs (11-09):** **THE TIERS ARE QUOTAS, NOT FEED TYPES** — every plan, Free included, has *all* the Job, Company, Semantic and Export APIs; they differ by jobs per month and refresh: **Free $0 — 500 jobs / mo, daily refresh, hard cap** · **Starter $99 — 25k / mo, hourly, hard cap** · **Growth $249 — 250k / mo, hourly, soft cap + $1.50 / 1k over** · **Scale $999 — 2M / mo, $1 / 1k over** · pay-as-you-go via Apify $3 / 1k · Enterprise (custom delivery, history back to 2023). **Billing is per job RETURNED** (a search with limit 100 that returns 100 uses 100), and there is a **free cost-estimate endpoint** — so **draft pays only for what its filter asks for; it never receives (or pays for) the low-value bulk.** **THE FEED IS A FILTER WE WRITE** (`POST /v2/jobs/search`, or `/v2/jobs/export` for big pulls with the same filters): **locations (country = United States)** · **job categories** · **job titles** · **keywords** (skills / tech, e.g. TypeScript, Kubernetes) · **experience level / years** · salary · company size · industries · **posted on or after a date / `days_ago`** · **first saved by Hirebase at or after a time** (for incremental sync) · **visa sponsorship true / false** (← the D185 beachhead, directly). **The expired-jobs feed is free** (identifiers only) — that's the removal path. **Technographics:** each listing carries a parsed tech stack; the Insights API's *technology demand* has 25 calls / mo included, then $10 / 1k.
**▶ THE FEED DRAFT WANTS (D140 P1, Hirebase first — the owner's lean, 11-09; the TheirStack trial becomes optional, run only if Hirebase's quality disappoints):** **(1) USA only** — `locations: [{country: "United States"}]` + remote-US. **(2) Only draft's categories** — Hirebase's job categories mapped onto `roles-v1.json`'s non-held categories (the map in `content/taxonomy/`), titles / keywords from the subcategories' aliases for precision; **never pull the categories D127 already excludes** (the blue-collar / "housekeeping" set the owner means — cleaning, retail floor, warehouse, drivers, food service) **and D127's leak rule + classifier still run on every Hirebase row** (Hirebase's own categories are imperfect: its docs' sample tags a civil engineer "Other"). **(3) A 60-day backfill, not 90, then incremental** — jobs older than ≈ 45–60 days are mostly filled or ghosted (D137); the backfill takes `date_posted ≥ today − 60`; after it, **hourly or nightly pulls by first-saved time** (only new rows), and the **free expired feed removes closed ones**; a job leaves draft when it expires or passes 90 days, whichever first. **(4) Don't pay twice for what the crawler has** — measure the overlap on the free tier; if large, aim the filter at what the crawler misses (other ATS families, companies not in `company_ats_list`) before paying. **(5) Hirebase's tech stack feeds D179 (5)** as one more evidence source per company (never the only one for a claim; never into D134's API — the licence). **(6) The visa-sponsorship filter powers D185-2's alerts and D185-6's pages** for the beachhead.
**SIZING BEFORE ANY CARD (agent, on the Free plan — zero cost):** with the filter above, call the **estimate endpoint** for: the 60-day backfill size · new matching jobs per day · the sponsorship subset; pull **the Free plan's 500 jobs** as a sample and report: share already in our crawl, share D127 holds, share dead on arrival (live check), field quality (salary, level, tech stack, apply link), and the category spread vs `roles-v1.json`. **Then the plan follows the numbers:** e.g. a backfill above 25k → **Growth ($249) for one month** (backfill + incremental), then drop to whatever the daily new-job rate needs (≈ 800 new jobs / day ≈ 25k / month fits Starter; more needs Growth). **No paid plan without the owner's yes on those numbers.** **TESTS:** `d140HirebaseUsaOnly` · `d140HirebaseCategoriesFromTaxonomy` · `d140HirebaseExcludedCategoriesNeverPulled` · `d140HirebaseLeakRuleStillRuns` · `d140HirebaseIncrementalByFirstSaved` · `d140HirebaseExpiredFeedRemoves` · `d140HirebaseSizingBeforeSpend`. **Owner (⏸):** make a **free Hirebase account** (no card) and put its key in `.env` as `HIREBASE_API_KEY` (and in Railway when the trial goes live); then read the agent's sizing report and say which plan, if any.

## ⛔⛔ [T2 SCREENS — a rule for every screen] D182 · ONLY USEFUL, NEW INFORMATION — no label restates what's already on the screen — 2026-11-07

✅ Owner 11-07: *"theres no need for Software engineering › Backend · Senior labels on the cards, no self explanatory, redundant info thats already there, not just this im saying all labels, only useful new info."*
**THE RULE (beside D149's "the sketch is the spec"):** **a label, chip, tag or caption appears only if it tells the person something they can't already read on that screen.** A job card's title already says *Senior Backend Engineer* — so no category, subcategory or level chip. **Keep a word only where the value would be ambiguous without it** (*86%* needs *match*; *$165k–$205k* does not need *salary*; *Hybrid* does not need *work mode*). **Useful and new stays:** the team's stack (*Works with Go, Kafka …*), the sponsorship history, liveness (*checked today*), the match. **The taxonomy drives filters, search, Atlas and the company page — it is never decoration on a card.** Sketch-only marks (the *NEW* tags in the D179 sketch) are never built. **Applies to every screen, existing ones too:** **⛔ Owner 11-07 carve-out: *"note that the job postings bubbles and utility buttons on hover stays."*** — **the bubbles that postings show today and the utility buttons that appear on hover are KEPT as they are**; D182 never removes them, and the inventory below lists them as *kept by the owner*, not as candidates. Only labels that restate what's already visible are in scope (e.g. the new taxonomy chip). The agent inventories labels that restate visible information (cards, rows, headers, empty states, section captions) on the jobs page, Home, Atlas, Interview, Profile and Admin → a list in NOW with screenshots, **the owner approves the removals**, then one pass removes them. **TESTS:** `d182NoTaxonomyChipsOnCards` · `d182UnitLabelsOnlyWhereAmbiguous` (a pinned list of the value cells that keep a word) · the screen pins updated on purpose.

## ⛔⛔ [T2 SCREENS × T8 ATLAS × T9 GROWTH] D179 · AN OPEN JOB BOARD, A PAGE FOR EVERY COMPANY, ONE TAXONOMY (category → subcategory) SHARED BY SEARCH, POSTINGS AND ATLAS, AND TECHNOGRAPHICS THAT EARN THEIR PLACE — 2026-11-07

✅ Owner 11-07: *"i want all the jobs open for everyone to see, and a company page and description for every distinct company, just like linked in. but for search and filtering, there would be categories and then sub categories, so SWE/SDE or software engineer and all the distinct software engineers as sub categories, this fits our model for atlas too for mapping which we can reuse to show on postings. so project manager, and then construction, media, technical as categories. the technographics has to slap though for this to work along with the mapping."*
**WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (so this extends, not restarts):** **D128 P1** — a public, server-rendered page per posting (`/jobs/<company>-<title>-<id>`, `JobPosting` JSON-LD, a jobs sitemap of 3,739, closed postings dropped) · **D127** — every posting classified to **one category + one occupation (SOC) + a level**, with a confidence; below it, **held** (never shown; leak rate 0) · Atlas's families (the 40 on *Your map*, `FAMILY_CATEGORY`) and per role / level posting counts (`atlas_role_level_stats`) · **a `company_technographics` table with no writer since A80 V4**, and a 31-company tool registry that duplicates it badly · logo providers failing (D170).
**(1) ONE TAXONOMY — `content/taxonomy/roles-v1.json`, the single source for search, postings and Atlas.** **Two levels: Category → Subcategory**, each subcategory mapped to its SOC occupation (compatibility with D127) and to its Atlas family. **⛔ The rule that keeps it useful: a subcategory exists only where the work — and so the skills — meaningfully differ.** That is what lets Atlas reuse it: every subcategory has its own skill set (from its postings), so it can be a node on the map and a role for D178's readiness %. Examples (the owner's): **Software engineering** → Backend · Frontend · Full-stack · Mobile (iOS / Android) · Embedded · Infrastructure / platform · SRE · DevOps · Security engineering · ML engineering · Data engineering · QA / SDET · Game · Graphics · Distributed systems … · **Project management** → Construction · Media and creative production · Technical / IT · Product delivery · Program management … (PM in construction and PM in media need different skills, so domain-flavoured subcategories are right here). **Titles are normalised into it:** *SWE, SDE, SDE II, Software Development Engineer, Member of Technical Staff → Software engineering* (+ the subcategory from the posting's content, not only its title). **The level stays a separate facet** (intern → principal; D106), not a subcategory. **Industry is a company facet, not a job category** (from the company page) — so *Backend at a fintech* is Category + Subcategory + the company's industry. **Open taxonomies to borrow from, after checking their licences in the D176 register:** O*NET (occupations, skills, alternate titles) and ESCO (EU occupations and skills, finer than SOC). **The chat assistant drafts v1 for the owner's review; nothing is built on it until approved.**
**(2) CLASSIFYING TO THE SUBCATEGORY:** D127's classifier gains the second level: category + subcategory + level + confidence. **D127's rule holds for the category** (unsure → held); **for the subcategory, unsure → shown at category level** (*"Software engineering · general"*) rather than held, so the board doesn't thin out. Backfill the board; Admin → Board shows counts per subcategory, the *general* share (target: small), and the daily spot-check sample per subcategory. **Shown on every posting** as a breadcrumb chip (*Software engineering › Backend · Senior*), each part a link to that filter / landing page.
**(3) THE OPEN BOARD — every shown job, browsable signed out:** `/jobs` (server-rendered, cached) with search, **Category → Subcategory filters with true counts** (D153 (2)'s counts fixed first), level, location / remote, posted date, sponsorship signal (D121), salary when given, **technology** (from (5)), company. Signed-out visitors can read and filter everything; **acting** (save, draft, apply, alerts) asks them to sign up. Held postings and closed postings never appear (D127 / D128). **No user data on any public page.** **Load:** public pages hit the read pool (A126) through a short cache; rate limits per IP; `robots.txt` allows the pages and the sitemaps, blocks the API. **Terms:** D128 P4 stands — each posting credits the employer and links the original; where a source forbids republishing descriptions, draft's reading + a short excerpt + the link.
**(4) A PAGE FOR EVERY DISTINCT COMPANY — `/companies/<slug>`:** **first, one company = one record** — entity resolution across sources (ATS board slug, website domain, normalised name; *Meta / Meta Platforms / Facebook* → one; parent and subsidiary linked, not merged), reviewed in Admin when unsure. **The page:** name, logo (fix the providers — D170), **About** (a short description in draft's own words, written from public facts — the company's own site, Wikidata (CC0) for industry / HQ / founded / size; the sources linked; **never copied from LinkedIn or any site whose terms forbid it — D78 stands**) · **open jobs** (by category → subcategory, with counts) · locations and remote · **hiring trend** (postings over the last 6 months, from our own crawl) · **sponsorship history** (US Department of Labor H-1B / PERM disclosure data is public; shown as *"filed N H-1B applications for software roles in 2025"* — strongly useful for OPT / international users) · **Tech stack** ((5)) · **what they ask for most** (top skills across their postings → Atlas lessons) · the ATS they use and the careers-site link · *"Follow"* (signed in; D159 trackers). **Structured data:** `Organization` JSON-LD; company pages in a sitemap. **An employer can ask for corrections or removal** — honoured within a day (D128 P4).
**(5) TECHNOGRAPHICS THAT EARN THEIR PLACE — evidence, never guesses:** **source 1 (the strongest, free, ours): the company's own job postings** — technologies extracted with the ATS vocabulary (`@draft/ats-scorer`) plus an alias table (*k8s → Kubernetes, Postgres → PostgreSQL, GCP → Google Cloud*); for each technology: **how many of their postings mention it, which teams / subcategories, first and last seen, trend** (new this quarter / fading) · **source 2: their public GitHub organisation** (languages and notable repos through GitHub's public API, within its terms) · **source 3: their public website** (front-end and infrastructure signals from headers and scripts — light, labelled as such) · **paid feeds (TheirStack, BuiltWith) only if the owner decides** — not needed for v1. **Shown as:** the company's *Tech stack* grouped (languages · frameworks · data · cloud · DevOps · ML / AI · tools), each item with its evidence (*"in 14 of 22 postings · last seen 3 days ago · Data, Platform"*); **"Your match"** for a signed-in person (*"you've proven 5 of their top 12"* → the missing ones as Atlas lessons); on each posting, *"this team works with …"*; **search by technology** (*"companies hiring for Kafka in Boston"*). Freshness window 180 days; nothing shown on fewer than 2 postings' evidence. **The `company_technographics` table becomes this, with a real writer on every crawl; the duplicate tool registry is retired.**
**(6) ATLAS REUSES ALL OF IT:** each subcategory is an Atlas role node (its skills from its postings) → D178's readiness % per subcategory (*"62% ready for Backend"*) · the map's families group subcategories · company tech stacks feed *"what they use → learn it"* · D177's Ask draft answers *"what does Stripe use?"* from the company page's evidence.
**(7) SEARCH ENGINES (D128 P2, widened):** landing pages per category, subcategory and location (*"Backend engineer jobs in Boston"*, *"Construction project manager jobs"*), and per technology where there are enough real jobs (no thin pages: a minimum count, or no page); company pages; IndexNow / Indexing API on change.
**PHASES:** **P0 measure** (report in NOW): D128's live state (pages, sitemap, indexing) · the current category spread and held share · **how many distinct companies, and how many duplicates** · the technographics table's state · logo coverage · **P1 the taxonomy v1** (chat assistant drafts; owner approves) · **P2 the subcategory classifier + backfill + the posting chip** · **P3 the open board** (filters with true counts) · **P4 company records + company pages** · **P5 technographics** (postings first, then GitHub, then website) · **P6 Atlas reuse** · **P7 landing pages + sitemaps**. **Sketch first** (chat assistant, on the owner's word): the open board with the two-level filter, and a company page with the Tech stack section. **OWNER DECISIONS:** (a) approve taxonomy v1 · (b) show H-1B / PERM history on company pages (recommended: yes) · (c) paid technographics feeds: not for v1 · (d) the public board shows full descriptions only where the source's terms allow (D128 P4 — a recheck per source). **TESTS:** `d179OneTaxonomySourceOfTruth` · `d179SubcategoryUnsureShowsCategory` · `d179HeldNeverPublic` · `d179PublicPagesNoUserData` · `d179FilterCountsTrue` · `d179OneCompanyOneRecord` · `d179TechNeedsTwoPostingsEvidence` · `d179AboutNeverCopied` · `d179ThinLandingPageNotPublished` · `d179RemovalRequestHonoured`.
**▶ 11-07 — P1 DRAFTED: `content/taxonomy/roles-v1.json` (status: DRAFT for the owner's review).** **23 categories (2 held per D127: healthcare, education) · 162 subcategories**, every one with SOC codes, an Atlas family, title aliases and distinguishing signals; ## ⛔⛔ [T5 ASSISTANT × T3 LEARNING] D177 · ASK DRAFT AS THE GUIDE TO ATLAS — a short, crisp answer, then the lesson that teaches it; every question Atlas can't answer becomes a content gap — 2026-11-07

✅ Owner 11-07: *"One idea i had was to leverage the ask agent to manoeuvre the site and Atlas material. So if i ask the agent a question say, how does cloud work, how is the data transmitted exactly, it should be able to answer with a brief explanation like a small crisp answer and then point to the course material to learn more about it. This will not only help the users but also help us fill the gaps from the unanswered asks of the users. Write it to the log."*
**WHAT IT DOES:** a learning question to *Ask draft* (D167's panel) gets **(1) a short, crisp answer** — a few sentences, plain words, no wall of text — then **(2) where to learn it properly in Atlas**: one to three cards that open the exact course → module → lesson (D172's library), each with its length and *Read / Watch / Try*, plus **(3) one next step** (*"Start this lesson"*, *"Take the 5-min check"*). Example: *"How does the cloud work? How is the data actually transmitted?"* → three or four sentences (your data is split into packets, sent over the internet using TCP/IP, encrypted in transit with TLS, and reassembled on servers in a provider's data centre) → cards for *Cloud fundamentals → Networking basics* and *→ How HTTPS works*. **The same panel also moves people around the site** (*"where are my saved answers?"*, *"open my résumé editor"*) — it opens the page, it doesn't describe it.
**HOW IT ANSWERS (built on D162's gateway and T5's rules):** answers come **from retrieval over Atlas's own material first** (decks, lesson summaries, the source register's open and share-alike items, the glossary), with the lesson ids it used; **links are only ever to lesson ids that exist** — the answer is checked before it's shown, and a card that doesn't resolve is dropped, never invented · when Atlas has nothing on the topic, it still gives the short answer from general knowledge, **marked as such** (*"Atlas doesn't have a lesson on this yet"*), and offers the nearest lesson if one is close · **⛔ D176 (5) applies: no text from a source whose `aiUse` is restricted (OpenStax) ever goes into the retrieval index or the model call** · **⛔ D173 (1) applies**: the question and the retrieved lesson text are fenced as data; nothing inside them can change what the assistant does · learning answers never award points (points stay proof-only, D172) and never claim a skill for the person (D169).
**THE GAP LOOP (the second half of the idea):** every learning question is recorded **with how well Atlas covered it** — `covered` (a lesson matched well) · `partial` (a lesson is near but doesn't answer it) · `gap` (nothing) — plus whether the person opened the lesson. **Admin → Atlas → Asks** groups them by topic (similar questions clustered), shows how many people asked, the pathway they're on, and the coverage; **the top gaps become the content backlog** — a gap is closed by a new lesson or deck slide whose sources come from D176's register, and when it ships the cluster flips to `covered`. A weekly line in Admin: *"Top 10 unanswered this week."* **Privacy:** questions are stored **without the person's identity** (no user id on the gap record; names, emails, companies and numbers stripped before storing), kept 90 days, used only to improve Atlas; one line in the privacy page and a *"Don't use my questions to improve Atlas"* switch in Profile → Privacy.
**WHAT IT NEEDS FIRST:** D162's gateway (the task `atlas_answer`, Haiku-class, with its own evaluation) · D173 (1) injection defence · D176-3 (every Learn item has a source id) and D176-5 (the AI-use guard) · lesson ids that are stable and deep-linkable (D172's course → module → lesson). It can start small: today's decks-v1 (8 decks, 40 slides) + the curated links are enough to answer and point for the CS pathways, and **the gap log is useful from day one even when most answers are gaps**.
**MEASURES:** share of learning questions `covered` / `partial` / `gap` by pathway · how often the lesson card is opened · how many gap clusters were closed each month · answer length (kept short: a cap, and an eval that marks long answers down).
**AGENT TASKS (T5, after the T1 / T7 order in NOW; starts with D176-3 and D176-5):** **D177-1** the `atlas_answer` task on the gateway: retrieve → short answer → lesson cards → one next step; links resolved against real lesson ids before showing · **D177-2** the site-navigation intents (open a page / a section; never act without confirmation, T5's rule) · **D177-3** the ask log with coverage, de-identified, 90 days, the opt-out switch · **D177-4** Admin → Atlas → Asks (clusters, counts, coverage, *top 10 unanswered*, link a cluster to the lesson that closes it) · **D177-5** the eval set: 50 real-style questions across pathways with the expected lesson(s) and a length cap. **TESTS:** `d177LinksOnlyToExistingLessons` · `d177ShortAnswerUnderCap` · `d177GapLoggedWithoutIdentity` · `d177OptOutRespected` · `d177RestrictedSourceNeverRetrieved` · `d177NoPointsFromAsks` · `d177UnknownTopicSaysSo`. **Sketch first:** the panel with an answer + two lesson cards, and Admin → Atlas → Asks — the chat assistant draws it on the owner's word.

## ⛔⛔ [T7 APPLY] D165 · THE SEMI-AUTO RUN FAILED — an audit of what actually ran, then the rules every run follows — 2026-11-06 · **PRIORITY: FIRST IN T7, BEFORE MORE UI**

✅ Owner 11-06 (screenshot: the tracker's *Prophetic Technologies Inc — Full Stack Software Engineer* (Ashby) in a modal: *HELD ON PURPOSE · Required fields were left empty · Still yours to answer: Resume, Salary Requirement · no resume on this attempt · Started 1:35:47 AM · Finished 1:35:49 AM · Attempts: 1 · No signal*): *"the semi run failed miserably, didnt even trigger a resume generation, couldnt care to show me the changes, dont know if it even attempted, the only thing it should ask me is unanswerable questions, that too because this is semi. for auto it will answer by agent with context or learn from answers given manually during initial period, i dont even know if the pdf toolkit changes i asked for even landed or if the prompt we modified is active now switched over from the previous one, and if the model has been switched to haiku, we need an audit to check these and also plan them on the ui side, task the audit to the agent."* **Chat assistant's reading of the screenshot:** the attempt ran **2 seconds** — résumé generation never ran (a tailoring call takes far longer), and the résumé field was then handed to the owner, which must never happen.
**THE AUDIT (agent, read-only first; every answer with evidence — commit, file:line, log line, config value, or a production read through the owner — reported as one table in NOW before any fix):**
**A1 · THIS ATTEMPT:** the posting, the application id, the attempt's full timeline from the logs — which pipeline steps ran, in what order, how long each took, and **why résumé generation did not run** (not called? skipped by a flag or mode? the base résumé read failing — D156 (6)? the new UI no longer triggering it — D164? the Ashby adapter not attaching?). **A2 · THE MODEL IN PRODUCTION:** for every model call (D162's task list), what production uses today — provider, model string, the prompt file and its version / hash, whether the call is *lean* or *full* (`DRAFT_TAILORING` and every related flag's live value), and whether **`prompts/bullet_craft.md` (D123 P6f) and the P6e prompt fixes** are what the live call actually loads. **Is résumé tailoring on Haiku in production, or still on the old model and prompt?** **A3 · THE PDF TOOLKIT:** which resume-master commit resumemaster.one serves; which version draft uses for résumé output; whether 44y's changes (`1b63282`, `3ef29de`, `7940c2f`: colon headings, header-only output, Download PDF, HTML → PDF) are live on both; whether draft's résumé PDF comes from that toolkit or another path. **A4 · THE ANSWERS:** for this attempt, every form field — its question, the answer used and **its source** (Profile · saved answer · routine answer by the model, D123 P7 · none) — and why *Salary Requirement* had none (no saved salary on the Profile?). **A5 · WHAT THE OWNER COULD SEE:** why the UI showed neither the résumé nor *What we changed* nor the steps that ran. **A6 · THE FIX LIST:** each finding → the fix, ordered; nothing fixed before the table is in NOW.
**THE RULES EVERY RUN FOLLOWS (from now; the fixes must satisfy them):** **R1 · THE RÉSUMÉ IS NEVER THE PERSON'S JOB.** Every run, SEMI or AUTO, **generates the tailored résumé (from the chosen base / job profile), attaches it, and shows it with *What we changed*** before anything else; if generation fails, the run stops with *"The résumé couldn't be made — Try again"*, never with "résumé left for you". **R2 · SEMI (*Ask me first*) STOPS ONLY FOR WHAT ONLY THE PERSON CAN ANSWER** — questions with no Profile value or saved answer that the model may not answer (D123 P7's never-list: eligibility, sponsorship, legal, EEO, **salary**, consent, human checks, numbers) — and **asks them inside draft, inline, in plain words** (*"What salary should we give Prophetic? · [ ] save it for similar jobs"*), never by sending the person to the employer's form; every answer given is **saved for next time** (scoped: per role / location for salary, global for eligibility); then the run continues by itself to **Ready to review** → the person presses **Submit**. **R3 · AUTO (*Apply for me*) ANSWERS FROM WHAT IT KNOWS:** the Profile, **the answers the person gave during their SEMI runs** (the "learn from answers given manually during the initial period" — the saved-answer bank R2 builds), and routine answers written by the model with context (D123 P7); ⛔ **items on the never-list are answered only from the person's own saved answers** — if there is none, AUTO holds that one application as *Needs you* rather than invent it (eligibility, salary and legal answers made up by a model are a real-world risk to the person). **R4 · EVERY ATTEMPT IS VISIBLE:** the tracker shows each attempt's steps as they happen — *read the posting → résumé tailored (what we changed) → résumé attached → n of m fields filled (each with its source) → waiting for you / ready to review → sent* — so "did it even try?" is always answerable at a glance. **TESTS:** `d165ResumeAlwaysGenerated` · `d165ResumeNeverLeftToUser` · `d165SemiStopsOnlyForNeverList` · `d165AskInlineInDraft` · `d165AnswersSavedForNextTime` · `d165AutoUsesSavedAnswers` · `d165AutoNeverInventsNeverListAnswers` · `d165AttemptStepsVisible` · `d165LiveModelAndPromptReported` (A2's table regenerated by a script, committed).
**THE UI — ✅ APPROVED 11-06 (owner: *"approved"*): `held-application-sketch.html`** (the owner saves it to `docs/sketches/`). The held application **opens in place in the tracker** (no modal, nothing blurred) in four states: **Needs you** — only the never-list question, asked inline (*"What salary should we give Prophetic?"*, a field, *"Use this for similar jobs (full-stack, US) next time"* ticked), a line confirming everything else is done, **Continue** · **The résumé couldn't be made** — *Try again* / *Pick another résumé*, nothing left to fill · **Ready to review** — **Submit** (the person's press) / *Edit an answer* · **Sent**; under each, **the steps the run took** (read the posting → tailored the résumé with *What we changed* → attached → filled n of m with *see the answers* → waiting for you → ready → sent), *The posting · Résumé · Answers* on demand with **each answer's source**, and one quiet line for an earlier attempt (*show*). Removed: *HELD ON PURPOSE*, *No signal*, *Hide 1 attempt*, *Open & fill*, raw URLs, the title repeated three times. **TESTS (add):** `d165HeldOpensInPlace` · `d165AnswerSourcesShown` · `d165EarlierAttemptsQuiet`.

## ⛔⛔ [T3 LEARNING] D169 · YOUR SKILLS LIVE IN ATLAS, ON THE SEMANTIC LAYER — and a skill is proven before it goes into a résumé — 2026-11-06 · ✅ **APPROVED BY THE OWNER 11-06 (*"yes, we can change this later, mark as such"*) — REVISABLE: the owner may change this split later**

**P1 · ONE *YOUR SKILLS* PANEL IN ATLAS, TWO VIEWS OF THE SAME DATA (chat assistant's proposal):** the semantic layer *is* Atlas (the skill graph, synonyms, families, the "leads to" links) and a person's skill is **a position on it** — so skills are managed where they're defined. **List** (manage: add · remove · prove; each skill resolved to its Atlas node, with its state *claimed · checked · built* and its proof) and **Map** (explore: the skills drawn against the market — what's near, what opens the most roles, the gaps for the target). One place, two views, nothing shown twice. **Profile** keeps the résumés, job profiles, saved answers, settings and connections, plus **one line linking to *Your skills* in Atlas**. A skill typed by the person is matched to its node (D105 / D134's resolve; an unknown one is held for the curator, never invented as a node).
**P2 · GATE THE USE, NOT THE ADDING (chat assistant's proposal):** a hard gate on adding would block people with real skills the question bank doesn't cover yet (≈ 15 roles so far), so: **adding stays open — a new skill lands as *claimed***; ⛔ **a skill that is not on the person's résumé is never written into a tailored résumé until it is proven**, by one of: **a quick check** (3–5 questions from D150's bank for that skill, ≈ a minute, inline, D142 Check's rules incl. extended time) · **a build** (D142 Close) · **a proof link** (D109); passing moves it to **checked** (or **built**). **No questions yet for that skill:** proof is a link or a build; until then it shows *not yet checked*, counts on the map, is **offered for Defend practice** (an interviewer will ask), and stays out of generated résumés. **The ATS panel's *You could claim* (D152 8) follows the same rule:** *That's true of me* opens the quick check in place (or the proof choice). This keeps D141's honesty rule and the claimed → checked → built ladder meaningful. **TESTS (if approved):** `d169SkillsPanelInAtlasListAndMap` · `d169ProfileLinksOnly` · `d169AddedSkillResolvesToNode` · `d169UnprovenNeverInResume` · `d169QuickCheckPromotes` · `d169NoQuestionsProofOrBuild` · `d169AtsClaimOpensCheck`.

## ⛔⛔ [T4 MODELS] D162 · THE MODEL GATEWAY — every feature asks for a task, a config picks the model, each task has its own evaluation; build on cheap and open models now, switch to our own when it passes — 2026-11-05

✅ Owner 11-05: *"what are the chances we can get everything built in parallel to our model training, the voice and chat bot, interview guide and assistant and link to it to an opensource or cheap model for now and switch when we have our own"* → the chat assistant's answer (below) → *"got it write these up, start a separate label for these tasks and note this change, each label would be its separate track … the log has to complete."* **Builds on D123 P3** (the provider-neutral client) and **D123 P5** (the open-model trial behind a flag). **Serves T5** (the assistant), **T6** (interview), **T3** (Learn's explanations) and every résumé task.
**THE ANSWER, RECORDED:** technically very likely — the switch is cheap *if this seam exists first*; building everything at once is the risk, not the technology (one founder, one coding agent, and every screen needs the owner's sketch approval). **What runs in parallel:** D160 P0–P1 (data, consent, fine-tuning — offline, never touches production) · the interview guides (mostly data and content). **What competes for the same build time:** the assistant and the voice coach. **Estimate:** staged in the TRACK ORDER, the assistant, the guides and a first voice coach can be working within a couple of months with high confidence; all at once beside T1's fixes, several would likely be left half-done.
**G1 · TASKS, NOT MODELS:** every model call names a task from one registry — `resume.gist` · `resume.bullets` (D123 P6) · `resume.summary` · `answers.routine` (D123 P7) · `assistant.chat` · `assistant.plan_action` (T5) · `interview.mock` · `interview.feedback` · `interview.example_answer` (T6) · `learn.explain` · `content.draft_for_review` (decks / questions / Atlas text the owner approves) — **no feature names a model.** **G2 · ROUTING BY CONFIG:** one config per environment maps each task → provider · model · parameters · fallback · budget; per-task rollout by cohort (**shadow** → a % → default); **a switch or a rollback is a config change**, applied without a deploy, recorded with who / when / why. **G3 · PER-TASK EVALUATION:** each task has its evaluation set and pass rule before any model takes it — résumé tasks: D123's harness (the owner's blind check, the guard pass rate, the ATS lift) · the assistant: answer correctness against retrieval, **action safety** (never acts without confirmation, never outside the user's scope) · interview: a rubric the owner rates on a sample · every task: cost and latency budgets (p50 / p95); a model **takes a task only when it passes**. **G4 · TELEMETRY:** per task × model: calls, tokens, cost, latency p50 / p95, errors, fallbacks — a card in Admin → System (D151 Rule 6). **G5 · PROVIDERS:** **now** Anthropic (Haiku default, Sonnet fallback) and OpenAI-compatible **hosted open-weight models** for cheap tasks (D123 P5's trial path); **later** self-hosted serving (vLLM / SGLang) when volume justifies it; **last** our own fine-tuned model (D160) task by task. **G6 · THE DATA LINE:** every stored model output carries its `source` (provider · model · version); **dataset builds refuse rows whose source is a Claude call** (D160 rule 1); if assistant transcripts are wanted for training later, a share of that traffic is routed to an open model whose licence allows training on its outputs, **with the user's opt-in**. **G7 · VOICE LATENCY:** T6's voice coach uses hosted speech-to-text / text-to-speech first and streams the interviewer's reply, because a conversation needs low latency; self-hosted speech comes later. **TESTS:** `d162NoFeatureNamesAModel` (a lint) · `d162RoutingByConfig` · `d162SwitchWithoutDeploy` · `d162RollbackInstant` · `d162ShadowBeforeDefault` · `d162PassRuleBeforeTakeover` · `d162TelemetryPerTaskModel` · `d162SourceTaggedOutputs` · `d162TrainingRefusesClaudeRows`.

## ⛔⛔ [T4 MODELS] D160 · OUR OWN MODEL — fine-tune an open model for résumé writing first, then the in-platform assistant; proved by our own evaluation before it replaces anything — 2026-11-05 · LOGGED, NOT SCHEDULED

✅ Owner 11-05: *"perhaps the most ambitious things I am planning to do is to have our own model, trained model. We basically have all the stuff we need, the data from thousands of job postings, the ATS stuff, the resumes, the content needed … to write the bullets within the resume … instead of an external LLM call. And this particular model should be capable of doing a bunch of stuff within the platform … be the personal assistant within the platform, to answer questions, to automate stuff within the platform, to be a chatbot basically … there have been a couple of recent breakthroughs … for inference … an Italian developer … open source … the new layered modeling … Soup … Unsloth Desktop."* **The tools, checked by the chat assistant 11-05:** **Unsloth Desktop** (open source, launched 11 Aug 2026; local running, fine-tuning — LoRA / QLoRA / full — dataset preparation, export) · **Soup** (open-source CLI, Apache-2.0; fine-tunes from one YAML; **layer streaming** trains up to 8B on a 4 GB GPU — BETA: text only, plain LoRA, specific architectures) · **ds4 / DwarfStar 4 by antirez** (the creator of Redis; a pure-C inference engine for one model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, 284B total / ≈ 13B active, Metal and CUDA — **requests served one at a time, alpha**: an experiment, not a multi-user server). **Reading (chat assistant):** "our own model" = **fine-tuning an open-weight model**, not training from scratch. **Fine-tuning teaches *how* to answer, not *what is true*:** bullet writing (style, the owner's bullet craft, D123's JSON edits) is a strong fine-tuning target; the assistant's knowledge comes from **retrieval + tools** over draft's own data and APIs, not from training.
**⛔ RULES FROM DAY ONE:** (1) **Never train on Claude's outputs** (Anthropic's terms; already recorded in D123 P5). draft's existing tailored résumés were largely written by Claude — they may be used **to evaluate** the model, **never to train it**. Training data: users' own résumés **with explicit opt-in consent and personal details removed**, examples written by the owner / curators, and outputs of open models whose licences allow training use (licence checked per model). (2) **A data register:** every dataset with its source, consent basis, licence and which model versions used it; **only consented, de-identified data is trained on** (a trained-in example can't truly be deleted later). (3) **Nothing replaces the current model until it passes D123's harness** (the owner's blind check, the guard pass rate, the ATS lift) **at lower cost per résumé**; Haiku / Sonnet stay as the fallback through D123 P3's provider-neutral client. (4) **Serving:** ds4-style single-model engines are for local experiments; production serving of a fine-tuned model uses a batching server (vLLM / SGLang) on rented GPUs — and **at today's volume the API may still be cheaper**; the cost comparison decides.
**P0 · DATA AND RIGHTS:** the register, an opt-in consent flow on the Profile (*"help improve draft's writing — your résumé, with your name and contact details removed"*), a de-identification pass (names, emails, phones, addresses, employers where needed), Claude-generated text excluded by its stored `source` flag, licences recorded. **P1 · ONE NARROW MODEL:** fine-tune an open 7–8B model (Soup or Unsloth, local GPU first) on the bullet / lean-JSON-edit task (D123 P2 / P6f); evaluate on D123's set vs Haiku; if it wins or ties at lower cost → **shadow mode** (both run, the user sees Haiku's) → route a share → default, with the fallback. **P2 · THE ASSISTANT:** a chat panel that answers questions from retrieval (the user's own data, draft's help, the Atlas) and **does things through draft's own APIs** (star, draft, change a setting, run a search) — **every action confirmed by the user first**, scoped to what the user can do, logged in an audit trail; it starts on an API model; consented conversations become future fine-tuning data. **P3 · DEEPER:** more tasks moved to the own model as each passes its evaluation; a larger model only when the data and usage justify it. **TESTS:** `d160NoClaudeOutputsInTraining` (a dataset build fails if any row's source is a Claude call) · `d160ConsentRequired` · `d160DeidentifiedOnly` · `d160DataRegisterComplete` · `d160ShadowBeforeSwitch` · `d160FallbackOnGuardFailure` · `d160AssistantConfirmsActions` · `d160AssistantAuditTrail`.

## ⛔⛔ [T6 INTERVIEW] D161 · THE VOICE INTERVIEW COACH — mock interviews you talk through, model answers you can listen to, and feedback on how you speak — 2026-11-05 · LOGGED, NOT SCHEDULED

✅ Owner 11-05: *"regarding the interview prep. We can have a voice model … a personal interview assistant to the users, so it can help them mock for their interviews and also guide them … how to approach each answer, how to answer the questions, how to approach the questions, how each round of it … talk to the agent one-on-one and have a conversation like they're having with the interviewer, or … do the reverse, ask the questions and get the answers, to listen to how the agent would answer it … pacing cues … pronunciations … good performance … with regards to speech. And I think this would be a game changer for us."* **Reading (chat assistant): no voice model needs training to start** — it's a pipeline of existing parts: **listen** (open speech-to-text) → **think** (the interviewer brain: D160's model or an API model, using the company guides and debriefs (D150 T12–T13), the question bank (D150 P1), Defend (D142) and the user's own résumé) → **speak** (open text-to-speech).
**MODES:** **(1) Mock interview** — pick the company, the round (recruiter screen · behavioural · coding talk-through · system design · the role's own rounds, PLAYBOOK A.3) and the level; the agent interviews, asks follow-ups on what was said, and ends with a written feedback report. **(2) Reverse mode** — the user asks, the agent answers; answers are **labelled as example answers**, built from the user's own résumé (never claims they can't make true — D141's honesty rule). **(3) Drills** — rapid questions under D142's timer rules, **with the extended-time setting and an untimed mode**. **(4) Review** — a replay of the session with the transcript and the notes on it.
**SPEECH FEEDBACK (from the transcript's word timestamps, no training needed):** pace (words per minute, against a comfortable range) · pauses · filler words · answer length · structure (situation · task · action · result) · how much of the answer used the posting's language truthfully. **Pronunciation is framed as clarity, never as accent:** many users are international; an accent is not a flaw, and the coach never suggests "reducing" one — only words a listener may mishear, offered gently and only if the user turns it on.
**PRIVACY:** voice is sensitive — explicit consent per session, recordings kept only as long as the user chooses (default: transcript kept, audio deleted after the review), **never used for training without separate opt-in** (D160's register), processed locally where the device allows.
**PHASES:** **P1** a desktop first version (speech-to-text → the interviewer brain → text-to-speech; mock + reverse modes for the 15 CS roles; the speech measurements; the feedback report) · **P2** drills, review, the company guides' rounds, phones · **P3** a custom voice, on-device processing, deeper tuning — only with the data and usage to justify it. **TESTS:** `d161ExampleAnswersLabelled` · `d161ExampleAnswersFromOwnResume` · `d161TimerRulesAndUntimed` · `d161ClarityNotAccent` (no accent-reduction wording anywhere) · `d161ConsentPerSession` · `d161AudioDeletedByDefault` · `d161NoTrainingWithoutOptIn`.

## ⛔⛔ D153 · THE BOARD BEHAVES — panels never overlap, filter counts add up, the posting facts never break, nothing is recomputed on a re-render — 2026-11-04

✅ Owner 11-04 (four screenshots: production's Location filter open with the posting panel drawn over it; the filter closed and the panel still stranded low until a scroll; the Home sketch with the dock over the deck and the fan over *Draft*; the workplace counts): *"the panels are not being adjusted dynamically as expected. They're overlapping when I open the filtering sentence … the panel identity is fixated. And then it only updates … the panel position after a mouse scroll … the filters are way off. The workplace says 52,000, and then remote 38,000, and then hybrid 36,000 … remote, hybrid, and on-site are making up for more than 100,000, but any workplace is just 52,000 … this is happening in all the filters … 40,000 jobs in California, 30,000 elsewhere … And then the font and the design of the filters revert back to the original one … the best fit analysis is being rerun on every re-render of the screen rather than that login session … as for the design i approve it but just make sure it doesnt overlap content over each other like in the ref image. and opening a posting or a card should [not] be flickering with a choppy rerender, it should be smooth, so i guess use the space and move content around smoothly."*
**(0) HOME IS APPROVED (D152)** — `home-sketch.html`, updated by the chat assistant 11-04 so that **nothing overlaps**: the dock **pushes the page right** while it's open (the page's left padding animates; it never covers the deck or the sentence); **the deck column reserves the fan's room** (the fan's sweep never covers Pass · Save · Draft or the right column); **opening a posting cross-fades in place** (the list stays mounted, the right column's height animates between the two, the list's scroll position is restored on Close). That sketch is the spec (D149).
**(1) LAYOUT INTEGRITY — NO PANEL EVER SITS ON TOP OF CONTENT.** **Cause (to confirm in code):** the posting panel's position is computed in JavaScript and refreshed only on `scroll`, so when the filter sentence opens or closes and the page above changes height, the panel keeps its old position. **Fix:** panels are placed by the layout itself — a grid column (or flex) with `position: sticky` inside its own column — **never by JavaScript offsets**; where anything must be measured, a `ResizeObserver` on the content, never a scroll listener. **Rules:** two panels never overlap (the dock pushes; the posting panel and the ATS panel live in their column; the filter panel pushes the content below it down); **no element moves except by animation** (opening / closing anything animates its height or position over ≤ 350 ms with `transform` / `opacity`; reduced motion: instant); **no flicker** — nothing is unmounted and remounted to open something; the posting's details are **prefetched on hover / focus** so opening is instant. **TESTS (Playwright, 1280 × 800 and 390 × 844):** `d153NoOverlapOpenFilter` (open each filter with a posting open → no two of {filter panel, posting panel, deck, list, dock} intersect) · `d153PanelFollowsWithoutScroll` (close the filter → the panel is in place in the next frame, no scroll needed) · `d153DockPushes` · `d153FanNeverCoversButtons` · `d153OpenPostingNoRemount` (the list's DOM node survives an open / close) · `d153ScrollRestoredOnClose` · `d153NoScrollPositionListeners` (a lint: no layout code in `scroll` handlers).
**(2) FILTER COUNTS THAT ADD UP.** **The cause, read from the owner's earlier screenshot:** the Domain panel said *"9,672 engineering · 43,009 with no kind of work on file, shown after"* — and 9,672 + 43,009 = **52,681, exactly the "engineering" count**: **every option's count adds the postings whose value is unknown.** The same pattern inflates workplace (remote + hybrid + on-site = 113k of 52k) and the other single-value filters; **location** additionally counts a multi-city posting under every city it lists, and probably a remote-only posting under every place. **Fix, per filter:** **single-value facets** (domain, workplace, employment type, level, sponsorship): an option's count = **postings known to have that value**; *any* = the total; and **options + unknown = total, exactly** (a test). The unknown stay visible as **one quiet line** (*"43,009 with no workplace on file, shown after"*) only while they exist — never inside an option's number. **Multi-value facets** (location): an option's count = postings that **list that place**, labelled as such (*"23,508 list California"*), each ≤ the total; **a remote posting counts under "Remote (US)"**, not under every city; a posting with no location counts in neither. Counts are computed by the background job (D151 Rule 2) for the current filter combination and cached, never by a full scan per open. **TESTS:** `d153SingleValueOptionsPlusUnknownEqualTotal` (every single-value facet, on the 100k fixture) · `d153UnknownNeverInAnOption` · `d153LocationCountsAtMostTotal` · `d153RemoteNotCountedPerCity` · `d153CountsFromJobNotScan`.
**(3) 82 % OF THE BOARD HAS NO CATEGORY — CLASSIFY THE BACKLOG.** The same screenshot shows **43,009 of 52,681 postings with no kind of work on file**: A112's 22× crawler boost brought in postings D127's classifier never processed. **Fix:** run D127's classifier (domain · occupation · level · workplace · employment type, with confidence) over the whole backlog **as a background job** (D151 Rule 2: batched, time-budgeted, resumable), and on every new posting at ingest; report the coverage per field in Admin → System (and in NOW after the first full pass). **Target: ≥ 95 % classified for domain and workplace**; D127's leak rule then applies again (low-confidence postings are held, not shown). **TESTS:** `d153BacklogClassifiedAsJob` · `d153CoverageReported` · `d153NewPostingClassifiedAtIngest`.
**(4) THE FILTERS KEEP THEIR ORIGINAL LOOK (owner: *"the font and the design of the filters revert back to the original one"*).** The filtering sentence and its filter panels keep **the original font and design they had before the recent restyle** — the serif sentence with the chosen words in ink, underlined in the brand orange; the panel's label, search box and option buttons with their counts — **only their counts (2) and their placement (1) change**; D147's restyle of the sentence is withdrawn. ⚠ *Chat assistant's reading of the owner's words — the agent shows a before / after of the sentence and one panel and waits for the owner's yes before changing them.*
**(5) THE FACTS BOX NEVER BREAKS A WORD.** Production shows the posting's facts cells squeezed into one row so words break mid-word (*"Rem / ote"*, *"not state / d"*, *"Says no spon / sors / hip"*). **Fix:** the cells wrap to a new row (flex-wrap, a minimum cell width, `overflow-wrap: normal`, no `word-break`), and **D152 (7) applies now**: *not stated* / *unknown* are omitted, not shown; a long value (*"Says no sponsorship"*) gets its own wider cell or is shortened in plain words (*"No sponsorship"*). **TESTS:** `d153FactsNeverBreakWords` (every cell's text measured at 1280 and 390) · `d153NoNotStatedCells`.
**(6) COMPUTED ONCE, NOT ON EVERY RE-RENDER.** **Observed:** the deck / best bets / match scores are recalculated whenever the owner navigates away and back. **Fix:** **(a) server:** a user's picks, best bets and match scores are **precomputed per user** (D151 Rule 2) and read with their `as_of`; they're recomputed **only when an input changes** — the résumé or Profile, a claim (the ATS panel), new postings arriving (in the background batch), the daily refresh — never because a screen was rendered; **(b) client:** responses are cached for the session (a query cache with a stale time; navigating back renders instantly from cache, then quietly checks for a newer `as_of`); a route change never triggers a recompute request. **TESTS:** `d153NoRecomputeOnNavigation` (navigate Home → Draft House → Home: zero recompute calls, the deck renders from cache in < 100 ms) · `d153RecomputeOnInputChange` (edit the résumé → one recompute) · `d153AsOfShownWhenStale`.
**ORDER:** (1) and (5) with the Home build (D152 — they're the same layout work); (2) + (3) now, as the board's data fix (they make every filter and count trustworthy; behind D151 Rule 1 only); (6) with D151 Rule 2's job system; (4) after the owner's yes on the before / after.
