## ⛔⛔ D151 · BUILT FOR SCALE — the server answers first and never does whole-board work while someone waits; proved at 100k and 500k postings — 2026-11-04

✅ Owner 11-04 (on the agent's live finding: *"Today's 05:25Z boot stalled for 50 seconds before the HTTP listener bound, which explains the 11-03 deploy-window 502s … The board jumped from 3,734 active postings to 81,510 in two days after A112's crawler boost, and the synchronous passes that scale with it now take tens of seconds"*): **"we have to look a permanent solution for this issue too."** The deck-bug investigation (NOW) fixes today's symptom; **this row makes it impossible to recur as the board keeps growing.** The board grew 22× in two days; the design must assume it grows 10× again.
**RULE 1 · LISTEN FIRST, THEN WARM UP.** The process binds the HTTP port **within 3 seconds of start**, before any work that reads more than a handful of rows. Boot = (1) config + open the database (WAL, `busy_timeout`) → (2) **migrations that are fast by construction** (schema only; any data backfill becomes a background job, never a migration step) → (3) **listen** → (4) everything else (Atlas recounts, precomputes, seed checks, cache warming, the crawler, the worker) starts **after** listening, as background jobs. **Two health endpoints:** `/api/health/live` (the process is up) and `/api/health/ready` (the database answers and the essential caches exist; until then it returns 503 with *"warming up"*); **Railway's healthcheck path is set to `/api/health/ready`** so a new deploy only takes traffic when it's ready and the old one keeps serving until then — **no more deploy-window 502s.** A boot timeline (each step's duration) is logged and shown in Admin → System.
**RULE 2 · NO REQUEST WAITS ON WHOLE-BOARD WORK.** ⛔ No request handler may run work whose cost grows with the number of postings (a full scan, a recount, a drain of an unbounded queue, a precompute). Such work moves to **one background job system**: a `jobs` table (kind · key · status · run_after · lease_until · attempts · last_error · duration) and a worker loop that leases jobs, runs them **in batches with a time budget** (e.g. ≤ 200 ms per slice, then yields), retries with backoff, and records duration; **one job per kind and key at a time** (dedupe). Requests read **precomputed results** (the last good one, with its `as_of`) and never block on a refresh; if a result is missing, they return the last good one or a clear "still preparing" state — never a spinner without end. Incremental beats full: the live counts (D118), the picks / best bets (D136), the ghost score (D137), Your market (D150 T09) update from change queues in bounded batches, with a nightly full recount only as a check.
**RULE 3 · THE EVENT LOOP STAYS FREE.** CPU-heavy work (scoring many postings, building large maps, parsing feeds) runs in a **worker thread or a child process**, not on the web server's event loop. **Event-loop delay is measured** (`perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay`) and shown in Admin → System; p99 above 100 ms for 5 minutes raises an Admin alert with the jobs running at the time.
**RULE 4 · THE DATABASE STAYS FAST AS IT GROWS.** **Writes in small transactions** (≤ 500 rows each) so the crawler never holds the write lock long enough to stall readers; **WAL checkpoints** on a schedule with the WAL size watched; **every query on a request path uses an index** (checked in CI with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` against the scale fixture: no full scans of `postings` on request paths); **active vs closed:** request-path queries read active postings through a partial index (or an active-only table), and closed postings older than D78's 120 days move to an archive table nightly, so the hot set stays the size of what users can apply to; **pagination everywhere** (no endpoint returns an unbounded list). **SQLite is kept** (one service, one volume): at this size it is fast when work is off the request path; **revisit a move to Postgres only when** the board passes ≈ 1 M active postings, or the web and worker must run as separate services, or write contention shows in the metrics — recorded here so it's a measured decision, not a reflex.
**RULE 5 · PROVED AT SCALE, IN CI, EVERY TIME.** The agent's throwaway "inflated copy" becomes **permanent**: `scripts/scaleFixture.mjs` builds a realistic database at **100k and 500k active postings** (plus users, applications, Atlas, Learn) from synthetic data — no real personal data. **A scale suite** (`npm run test:scale`, in CI on every pull request at 100k, nightly at 500k) asserts: **boot to listen ≤ 3 s** and to ready ≤ 30 s; **p95 ≤ 300 ms** for the deck, Full House, the posting, the tracker, Your map, the résumé check and Admin → Testers; **event-loop p99 ≤ 100 ms** under 20 concurrent users; **no request-path full scan**; **every background job finishes its slice within budget**. A pull request that breaks a budget fails.
**RULE 6 · SEE IT WITHOUT SHELL ACCESS TO PRODUCTION.** Today the agent's read-only production check was (rightly) refused by its permission mode. Instead of opening shell access, **Admin → System** (owner-only) and a matching owner-only diagnostics endpoint show: the last boot's timeline, event-loop delay, the slowest endpoints (p50 / p95 / p99, last hour and day), the job queue (backlog per kind, oldest waiting, failures), active / closed / archived postings, database and WAL size, the crawler's last run. The agent reads these through the owner (or a short-lived read-only diagnostics token the owner issues from Admin, scoped to that endpoint only, expiring in 24 h) — **never through production shell access.** **Growth alarm:** active postings up > 50 % in a day, or the database up > 1 GB in a day, raises an Admin alert (A112's 22× jump should have been one).
**ORDER:** (1) **Rule 1 + the Railway healthcheck** (ends the 502s) → (2) the scale fixture + the scale suite in CI (so every later fix is measured) → (3) Rule 2's job system, moving each whole-board pass found by the agent's trace into it, one at a time, each proved by the suite → (4) Rule 3 (worker thread for heavy scoring) → (5) Rule 4 (small write transactions, partial index, the archive) → (6) Rule 6 (Admin → System, the diagnostics token, the growth alarm). Steps 1–2 come **right after the deck bug's root-cause report**, before D149's screens. **TESTS:** `d151ListenWithin3s` (100k fixture) · `d151ReadyGatesTraffic` · `d151NoMigrationBackfill` · `d151NoWholeBoardWorkOnRequestPath` (a guard: request handlers that touch `postings` without a bounded, indexed query fail the test) · `d151JobsLeasedBatchedBudgeted` · `d151OneJobPerKindKey` · `d151LastGoodNeverSpinner` · `d151EventLoopP99Under100ms` · `d151SmallWriteTransactions` · `d151NoFullScanOnRequestPaths` · `d151ArchiveClosedPostings` · `d151ScaleSuiteBudgets` (100k on PRs, 500k nightly) · `d151DiagTokenScopedExpiring` · `d151GrowthAlarm`.

## ⛔⛔ D150 · ONE LOOP — what the competitors each sell separately, joined into draft; the quiz is the learning engine, and the 3-minute audit is the front door — 2026-11-03

✅ Owner 11-03, after researching competitors (33 screenshots in `Downloads/draft-research`: TripleTen's skills audit and programme, newline's webinar funnel, Hello Interview's guides, A Life Engineered, AlgoMap, Interview Kickstart; plus LeetCode): *"the quiz idea, career guidance, mapping, assessments, interview guides specific to companies, leet code already has these too. so in the scope and direction of our platform, go ahead and do a deep analysis to see where each of these fit into our products and how to shape them for one seamless product"* · *"i was also hoping we can use the quiz part as part of our own learning model. anyhow write this plan and execution up in detail into the worklog to pick up."*
**WHAT THE RESEARCH SHOWED (chat assistant's analysis, 11-03):** five patterns — (1) **a short diagnostic as the front door** (TripleTen: a target role with real pay + requirements, then **scenario questions that test judgment** — *"your monolith has grown, teams keep blocking each other, your first architectural move?"* — ending *"see where you stand, what closes the distance"*; AlgoMap's 9-question quiz) · (2) **market data as the hook** (Interview Kickstart: *"AI Engineer postings up 2.4× — see which role fits your background"*) · (3) **company interview guides by level** (Hello Interview: stages as a table, the recruiter call, *"living document, report an issue"*, free tracks + Premium) · (4) **"build on what you have" in steps** (TripleTen's five steps, *"same foundation you already have, one tier of systems on top"*) · (5) **proof and side doors beat the résumé** (newline). **Almost all are funnels into an expensive programme or coaching; none applies for you and none measures what happens after an application** — the gap draft fills. ⛔ **Not adopted:** their unverified ad numbers, guarantees (*"promotion or we work for free"*), or any of their content (link to it, or build from our own data).
**THE LOOP (the product, end to end — every module is a step, never a separate app):** **1 · See where you stand** (résumé + the audit → Your map, D116) → **2 · Choose where to go** (the navigator, D143, from live market data — options ranked, the person decides, D135) → **3 · Get there** (the route: Learn pieces D117, builds D142 Close, practice D142 Play) → **4 · Prove it** (claimed → checked → built → defended; proof links D109) → **5 · Land it** (best bets D136, ghost score D137, warm paths D138, auto-apply D113 / D146) → **6 · Win the interview** (the company guide, Defend D142, the debrief D110) → back to 1 (careers continue — why the subscription outlives one search). **Positioning:** *"Others sell you a quiz, then a $5,000 programme. draft gives you the diagnosis, the route, the practice, the referrals and the applications, in one place."*

**P1 · ONE QUESTION BANK, USED EVERYWHERE — the quiz as the learning engine (owner: *"use the quiz part as part of our own learning model"*).** **Item schema** (`learn_questions`, versioned like `learn_content`): `id · skills[]` (Atlas node slugs) `· pieces[]` (Learn step ids) `· role_families[] · level` (entry / mid / senior) `· type` — **scenario** (a situation + 3–4 choices, judgment; TripleTen's form) · **recall** (short, for 10-second timed rounds) · **explain** (open, own words, never auto-graded) `· stem · choices[] · correct · why[]` (**an explanation for EVERY choice**, the right and the wrong — the learning is in the *why*) `· source` (owner · drafted-for-review) `· status` (draft · live · retired) `· stats` (answered, share correct, median time — difficulty comes from real answers). **Who writes them:** the owner, or the chat assistant drafts batches **for the owner's review** (the D105 P11 pattern) — **nothing goes live unreviewed** (a wrong answer key destroys trust); Admin → Learn → Questions: list, edit, approve, retire, see each item's stats; items with a suspicious share correct (> 95 % or < 15 %) flagged for review. **Where the same bank is used:** **the audit** (P2) · **Check** (adaptive per skill, D142) · **Play** (timed rounds, daily challenge, D142) · **Learn** — **each piece gets 3–5 questions**; a piece's earned bar (D117 C8) gains **"checked"** — *opened · checked (its questions passed) · explained (own words) · built* — and Your map's states follow (*claimed → checked → built*); **wrong answers schedule the piece again** (spaced review: 1 day → 3 → 7 → 21; one quiet *"3 to review"* line, never a nag) · **Defend** (the explain items about the user's own bullets) · **the company guide** (P4: the topics a company's interviews cover link to their questions). **Results are self-awareness, never a certificate** (D142's timer rules and accessibility apply: extended time, untimed practice).

**P2 · THE 3-MINUTE AUDIT — the front door, signed in or not.** At `/audit` (and offered before "Upload a résumé" to new users; the trial can use it too): **(1) pick a target role** (from the board's real roles in the user's field) → **its real card from OUR data**: median pay range from live postings, the top 3 requirements, open postings this week (*"market data, not a promise"*) → **(2) 6 scenario questions** for that role and the chosen level, one at a time in D145's type (the eyebrow skill, the scenario as the headline, the choices as large buttons; the *why* shown after each answer, briefly) → **(3) where you stand**: a few stat cards (*"strong on data modelling, weaker on streaming"*), *"what closes the distance"* (2–3 Learn pieces / builds, from the questions missed), and **jobs you could win now** (best bets for that role) → **(4) keep it**: sign up / upload a résumé to save it and start the route (the result attaches to the new account). **No résumé needed to take it; nothing kept without sign-up except anonymous counts.** **Shareable result line** (*"I'm 4 of 6 on the Senior Data Engineer bar"*) with the user's choice. **First content:** **3 target roles × 6 scenario questions × 2 levels** (≈ 36 items) in the owner's main fields (proposal: Data Engineer, Backend Engineer, ML Engineer), then more by demand.

**P3 · "YOUR MARKET THIS WEEK" — our own data as the hook.** From the board and the Atlas (D118 live counts): **roles rising / falling** (postings this week vs the last 4), **skills rising toward senior** for the user's role, **companies hiring most** in their field, **the ghost-job rate** by field (D137, aggregated) — one card at the top of the Atlas home (D120) for signed-in users, and **a public weekly page per field** (D128's SEO; the Skills Index). Numbers only from our data, with the date and the method one press away.

**P4 · COMPANY INTERVIEW GUIDES, GROWN FROM OUR OWN USERS.** When an application becomes an interview (D103 / D112 detects it), **the guide for that company and level opens with the Prep tab** (D110): **the stages** (as a table: recruiter call · screen · onsite rounds · final), **what the rounds cover**, **the topics, linked to their Learn pieces and questions**, **what people asked** (from debriefs), **dates seen**. **Sources, in order of trust:** (a) **our users' debriefs** (D110: after an interview, a 2-minute debrief — rounds, topics, questions in their words, outcome; consented to be pooled anonymously, never named; k-anonymity ≥ 3 before a company's guide shows debrief content) · (b) public facts the owner / curator has checked (the company's own careers / interview-process pages, linked) · (c) nothing else — **no copied third-party guides**. *"Living guide — report something wrong"* on every guide. Start with **the 20 companies our users apply to most** (Admin data).

**P5 · THE ROUTE SHOWN AS A STACK (presentation for D143):** the user's **foundation at the bottom** (*"your 5 years: Python, SQL, Spark, AWS"*) and **the steps stacked on top**, each a short title + 2–3 plain bullets of what you'll be able to do, numbered, the current one lit — TripleTen's clearest idea applied to our navigator; each step opens its Learn pieces / builds / questions.

**MILESTONES (sequenced by what each proves — not a calendar; the owner asked "why 90 days": it was only a planning habit):** **M1 · the bank + 36 reviewed items** (P1 schema, Admin review, the stats) → **M2 · the audit live** (P2) — *proves*: do visitors finish it (target ≥ 60 %) and sign up after (target ≥ 20 %)? → **M3 · quizzes inside Learn** (P1: 3–5 questions on the 20 most-routed pieces, the "checked" state, spaced review) — *proves*: do people come back to review? → **M4 · Your market this week** (P3) — *proves*: do the public pages bring visits? → **M5 · company guides** (P4: debriefs on, the top 20 companies seeded with checked public stages) — *proves*: do debriefs come in (target: 1 in 3 interviews)? → **M6 · the route as a stack** (P5). Each milestone's numbers land in Admin (D131's style) before the next starts. **Depends on:** D142 (Check / Play / Defend) and D117 (Learn) — P1 is their shared content layer; D110 for P4; D143 for P5; D149's fidelity rule for every new screen.

## ⛔⛔ D136 · BEST BETS — a precision shortlist: the few jobs to apply to this week, ranked by the chance of a real conversation — 2026-11-02

✅ Owner 11-02: *"Nobody has built a tool that tells you which 5 jobs to apply to this week — not 500, not 50 — based on your actual probability of getting an interview at each specific company. Ghost score, profile fit against real requirements, company hiring velocity, your network connections there. A ranked shortlist, not a firehose … the bottleneck has never been applications. It's qualified conversations."* **This becomes the top of draft's funnel** (the deck's first view, the picks of D113, the trial's 10 picks).
**P1 · THE SCORE — honest about what it is:** until outcomes calibrate it (P3), it is a **ranked "best bets" score built from signals, never called a probability**; shown as *Best bet · Good bet · Long shot* with its reasons. **Hard filters first (never ranked, simply out):** eligibility (D104 / D121: citizenship, clearance, "won't sponsor" for those who need it), category (D127), closed / dead postings (D137). **Then the signals, each with a stated weight in one file the owner tunes:** fit against the posting's **must-have** requirements (D123 P6a's job block — must-haves weigh more than nice-to-haves) · the real level (D106) vs the user's · **freshness** (hours since first seen; earlier is better) · **the ghost score** (D137) · **company hiring velocity** (from the crawl: postings opened and closed in the last 90 days, time-to-close) · **a warm path** (D138) · the user's aim (D143). **The card shows why:** *"Best bet: you're eligible · posted 9 hours ago · 13 of 15 must-haves · they closed 6 similar roles in 60 days · an alum works there."*
**P2 · THE SHORTLIST:** **"This week's best bets"** — default **5** (the user sets 3–20), refreshed as postings arrive; the rest of the board stays one press away (*"See all 214 matches"*); FULL AUTO and picks draw from the shortlist first.
**P3 · CALIBRATION — THE MOAT:** every application's outcome (D103 / D111: reply · interview · rejection · silence after 30 days) is recorded against the signals it had when sent; **monthly, the weights are refit** on real outcomes (logistic regression on the signals, holding out a test month), and **only once ≥ 500 outcomes exist** does the card show a calibrated *"≈ 1 in 6 chance of a reply"* — with the method in a tooltip. Until then, signals only. **TESTS:** `d136HardFiltersOut` · `d136ReasonsOnCard` · `d136WeightsOneFile` · `d136ShortlistDefaultFive` · `d136NoProbabilityUntilCalibrated` · `d136OutcomeRecordedWithSignals` · `d136RefitHoldout`.

**✅ P1–P3 BUILT 11-02 (44i, agent) — `a3a49d7`, LOCAL.** `shared/bestBets.js` (the weights, bands 70 / 50, shortlist 3–20 default 5), `services/bestBets.js`, `GET /api/best-bets`, `client/src/components/BestBets.jsx` on the ALL board. Signals built: must-haves (D123's split, now `splitMustNice`), level, freshness, ghost (D137), company closings in 60 days; warm path (D138) and aim (D143) weigh nothing until built — an unknown signal leaves both sides of the sum. Hard filters: not eligible by what the user set, won't sponsor for a needer, closed, already drafted / applied. Picks rank by the best-bet score before the ATS match. P3: migration 214 `application_signals` written at `writeApplication`; `refitBestBets` on the 1st (held-out month, ≥ 500 outcomes, kept only if it beats the average); the card shows no chance yet even after a fit — ⛔ **the owner approves that wording first**. Tests `d136BestBets` (9). ⚠ Not walked signed in.

## ⛔⛔ D137 · THE GHOST SCORE — likely-dead postings scored with evidence; only the provably dead are hidden — 2026-11-02

✅ Owner 11-02: *"ghost jobs … the problem with this is its guess work, and if we're wrong users lose an opportunity so we have to hit the target with this."* **Extends D107 (liveness).** ⛔ **Only a posting that is provably closed is hidden** — removed from the company's own careers site / ATS, or its apply endpoint refuses. **Everything else is scored and RANKED DOWN, never removed**, with the reasons shown and the user free to apply.
**P1 · SIGNALS (each with evidence the user can read):** age since first seen (*"open 94 days"*) · repost history (same company + near-same title / description re-listed: *"reposted 4 times since June"*) · mass duplicates (the same text posted to many locations) · **"evergreen" / "talent pool" / "future opportunities" wording** · the company's hiring velocity (D136: postings that never close) · a requisition id reused · **user reports** (*"applied, no reply in 30 days"* — one press on The Table) · **outcomes** (postings whose applications from draft never get a reply, P2).
**P2 · THE SCORE:** *Likely hiring · Uncertain · Likely not hiring* + the evidence; **calibrated on outcomes** (D136 P3's data: replies per posting vs its signals) — the threshold for *"Likely not hiring"* is set so that **fewer than 1 in 20 postings it flags ever produce a reply** (measured monthly; if it misses, the threshold rises). **The user's control:** a filter *"Hide likely not hiring"* (off by default); best bets (D136) rank them low automatically.
**P3 · PUBLIC:** the score appears on public job pages (D128) and in the Skills Index (opportunity #2 of 11-01) as a monthly ghost-job rate by company and category — aggregated, never naming a posting as fake. **TESTS:** `d137OnlyProvablyClosedHidden` · `d137EvidenceShown` · `d137RankedDownNotRemoved` · `d137FalseFlagRateUnder5Pct` (on outcomes) · `d137UserReportOnePress` · `d137FilterOffByDefault`.

**✅ P1 + P2 BUILT 11-02 (44i, agent) — `5a84c48`, LOCAL; migration 213.** `shared/ghostScore.js` (weights, Uncertain ≥ 2, Likely not hiring ≥ 5), `services/jobs/ghostScore.js` after D107's rollup (04:00 + the boot cleanup). User reports = The Table's existing one-press "Still nothing" (manual no_response) — no new button. Measured on the A111 crawl copy (12,514 active): 0.9 s; 5 Likely not hiring, all self-declared talent pools; 1,477 Uncertain ("open 90+ days"). The first text pattern caught real roles (Stripe, IMC, Anthropic) — tightened, pinned. P3 not built; "apply endpoint refuses" not checked. Tests `d137GhostScore` (10).

## ⛔⛔ D142 · READINESS — four modules: CHECK (where you really stand) · CLOSE (build what's missing) · PLAY (timed quizzes and riddles) · DEFEND (answer for your claims on the spot) — 2026-11-02

✅ Owner 11-01 / 11-02: *"candidates write resume bullets sophisticatedly using ai but fail to back it up in interviews due to lack of hands on experience … the foundational basics courses wont cut it for experience level probing and scrutiny … not just certification but something they can build … broken into bits … build a calculator for example but also each function and face the problems that arise and overcome them"* · *"split into modules: one that tests them to make them aware, one that can help them close the gaps, and quizzes and riddles, timed ones … they cant use ai to beat a 10 sec timer. Especially if we want them to defend their answers then and there."*
**CHECK:** a short adaptive diagnostic per skill the user claims or aims for (from the résumé + Your map); harder on right answers, easier on wrong; 5–10 minutes; the output is **awareness, not a grade** (*"syntax and data structures strong; memory and references weak — what senior interviews probe"*); each skill gets a state on Your map: **claimed → checked → built**. **CLOSE:** **builds broken into steps, each step a real problem met and solved** (the owner's calculator: add → floating point · precedence → parsing · brackets → recursion / a stack · big numbers → overflow · undo → state · bad input → errors), and deeper builds for experienced engineers (an HTTP server from sockets, a crash-safe key-value store, a rate limiter, a tiny git, a neural net without ML libraries, a query engine, a load balancer) — **"build what people normally import"**; a step is done only when **its tests pass** (D117 C8's earned rule); **driven by the user's résumé and aim** (*"your bullet claims Kubernetes at scale; no evidence; senior postings ask for it 48 % of the time; this 6-step build earns it"*); plus D115's Learn pieces for foundations. **PLAY:** **timed rapid rounds (10 s recall)**, **60–90 s reasoning** questions, **CTF-style riddles** (each answer unlocks the next), a daily challenge, streaks, opt-in leaderboards with friends. **DEFEND:** draft picks a bullet from the résumé or a finished build and asks the interviewer's follow-ups (*"what was the bottleneck? why that fix?"*), **timed, typed or spoken** (spoken defence is the hardest to fake), then a harder follow-up.
**THE TIMER'S RULES:** it blocks the easy look-up and tests what interviews test; it is NOT cheat-proof — so CHECK / PLAY results are **self-awareness, never a certificate**; anything ever shown to employers needs a proctored or live format (later). ⛔ **Accessibility:** an **extended-time setting and an untimed practice mode**, never penalised. **CONTENT:** a question bank per skill (tagged difficulty + concept), the first **10 most-claimed skills** in users' fields; questions written by the owner / curators, model-drafted only **for review** (an answer key that is wrong destroys trust); builds and riddles hand-curated, few and excellent, from one template (steps, the problem each introduces, tests, probe questions). **RUNTIME:** in-browser where possible (e.g. Pyodide for Python), a sandboxed runner for other languages later (a security surface — reviewed); hints through the user's own Claude via the connector (no model cost to draft). **REWARDS (later, recorded):** a **draft level** earned mainly by checked skills and finished builds (not by quiz volume); **seasonal build sprints**; the win that matters is an **opportunity** — sprint leaders introduced to companies sponsoring the sprint (the first employer revenue and the first earned reverse match). **TESTS:** `d142CheckAdaptive` · `d142MapStatesClaimedCheckedBuilt` · `d142StepDoneOnlyOnTests` · `d142BuildFromResumeGap` · `d142TimedModesAndUntimed` · `d142ExtendedTimeNeverPenalised` · `d142DefendFollowUps` · `d142NotACertificate` · `d142QuestionsReviewedBeforeLive`.

**✅ CHECK BUILT 11-02 (44i, agent) — `cde9e8d`, LOCAL; migration 217.** `services/readiness.js`, `/app/atlas/check` (`ReadinessCheck.jsx`), Admin → Data → Readiness questions (`adminReadiness.jsx`). The server times each question; timed answers past the limit earn no credit; extended (×2) / untimed never penalised; summary by concept, "not a grade or a certificate". ⛔ **20 drafted questions (SQL 10, Python 10) are DRAFTS — the owner reviews each answer key before anything is live.** Not built: CLOSE, PLAY, DEFEND; questions for the other 8 most-claimed skills. Tests `d142Readiness` (7).

## ⛔⛔ D134 · ATLAS AS ITS OWN MODULE — its own domain model, its own data, a versioned contract API; draft becomes its first consumer — 2026-11-01

✅ Owner 11-01: *"the biggest next thing is the atlas as a separate module with its contract api and separate domain model, i want it offered as a standalone thing offered into draft as an api."* **Goal:** Atlas (the graph, the thesaurus, the live stats, Learn, Your map) can be offered on its own — to other apps, schools, partners — while draft consumes it **only through its API**, like any other customer.
**THE BOUNDARY RULES (from day one):** ⛔ **Atlas never reads draft's database; draft never reads Atlas's** — only the contract API and its event feed. ⛔ **Atlas holds no personal data:** no names, emails, résumé text or applications; a user is an **opaque subject id** the consumer chooses; skill lists sent for a map are used for that call and not stored (progress is stored against the subject id only). ⛔ **One thesaurus, owned by Atlas** (today's `skill_synonyms` + aliases) — draft's ATS keeps a **versioned local snapshot** of it for speed and updates from the change feed, never a second copy that drifts.
**THE DOMAIN MODEL (Atlas's own):** **Node** (kind: role · skill · tool · concept · pattern · stack; slug, name, definition + who wrote it, status, **category / family** per D127) · **Alias** (the thesaurus) · **Edge** (typed: alias_of, part_of, requires, used_with, alternative_to, leads_to; source) · **Resource** (url, kind, level, hours, cost, checked_at, thumbnail — D119) · **WikiSummary** (cached, attributed) · **Stats** (postings per node / role / level / category, co-occurrence, mid → senior shares — **fed by posting events from consumers**, D118's live counts moved behind the API) · **Learn**: Content (versioned), Piece (needs, opens, teaches), Item, Checkpoint, Route · **Subject progress** (opened / explained / built per item, the C8 rule → **learned** nodes, D116 M8) · **Map** (computed, not stored: D116 M1's tree for a subject's skills + aim).
**THE CONTRACT — `contract/atlas/v1` (OpenAPI 3.1, in the repo; additive changes only within v1, a breaking change means v2):** **read** — `GET /v1/nodes/{slug}` · `GET /v1/search?q=` (D-normalised search) · `GET /v1/peek/{slug}` (D114's popup) · `GET /v1/graph/{slug}?depth=` · `GET /v1/families` · `GET /v1/roles/{slug}` (role page data) · `GET /v1/thesaurus/snapshot` + `GET /v1/changes?since=` (the feed: node / alias / edge / stats changes, cursor-based) · **compute** — `POST /v1/resolve` (terms → nodes, aliases, **broader terms**, sibling candidates — D123 P6c) · `POST /v1/annotate` (a posting's text + its extracted skills → the D114 link spans) · `POST /v1/map` (skills + role + level + aim → the tree, the three facts, the route — D116) · `POST /v1/learn/route` (targets → ordered pieces, D117 C5) · **events in** — `POST /v1/events/postings` (posting added / updated / closed: id, category, level, matched terms — the consumer's matcher output, so Atlas never needs the posting text it doesn't own) · **Learn** — `GET /v1/learn/content` · `GET /v1/learn/pieces/{id}` · `PUT /v1/subjects/{subject}/progress` · `GET /v1/subjects/{subject}/state` (finished pieces, learned nodes) · **admin (scoped keys)** — nodes, edges, resources, publish, Find on Wikipedia, Draft definitions, Learn import / review (today's Admin → Atlas tools, moved behind the API).
**AUTH, LIMITS, VERSIONING:** an API key per consumer (draft = the first), scopes (read · compute · events · learn · admin), rate limits per key, ETags + `Cache-Control` on reads, request ids; errors in one shape; latency budgets (peek / resolve p95 ≤ 100 ms from draft). **Consumer-driven contract tests:** draft's expectations of the API are tests that run against Atlas in CI; the OpenAPI spec is validated on every response in tests.
**THE MATCHER:** today's `postingMatcher` (with the boilerplate fix) becomes a **versioned package `packages/atlas-matcher`** (pure: text + thesaurus snapshot → matched terms) used by draft's ATS and by any consumer; Atlas publishes the snapshot it pairs with.
**WHERE IT RUNS:** a new Railway service **`atlas`** in draft's project (own database + volume), reached by draft over Railway's private network; the public Atlas pages (`/atlas/*`, SEO, D105 / D128) stay in draft's frontend, rendered from the API; a public API host (e.g. `api.jobsviadraft.com/atlas`) only when the owner decides to offer it externally.
**THE PATH (each phase ends with the suite green and the owner's walk):** **P0 · boundary audit** — `docs/ATLAS_BOUNDARY.md`: every place draft reads or writes an Atlas table (file:line), every place Atlas code reads a draft table, the thesaurus's readers; nothing changed. **P1 · the contract on paper** — the domain model and `contract/atlas/v1/openapi.yaml`, reviewed by the owner (and the chat assistant) **before any move**. **P2 · in-process module** — `packages/atlas` with its own DB handle and its own tables (moved by a migration), draft calling it only through a client that speaks the contract (in-process transport first); a lint rule fails CI on any import across the boundary. **P3 · its own service** — the same client switched to HTTP; dual-run in staging, comparing responses; events wired; the snapshot + feed for the ATS. **P4 · cutover** — draft's Atlas tables dropped after a verified export; rollback plan written. **P5 · offered outside** — public docs, keys, usage metering, pricing (the owner's call).
**STATUS (44f, 11-02):** ✅ **P0 written** — `docs/ATLAS_BOUNDARY.md` · ✅ **P1 written, AWAITING THE OWNER'S REVIEW** — `contract/atlas/v1/openapi.yaml` + `contract/atlas/v1/README.md` (§ 7: Q1–Q6). P2 has not started.
**ORDER:** after the current queue (the trial / survey work, D131, D125, D123's remaining parts); **P0 + P1 can start now** (documents only, no risk to the testers); P2 onward waits for the owner's review of P1. **TESTS:** `d134NoCrossDbAccess` (lint + runtime guard) · `d134ContractValidates` (every response vs the OpenAPI spec) · `d134ConsumerContractDraft` · `d134NoPersonalDataInAtlas` · `d134OneThesaurusSnapshotFeed` · `d134MatcherPackageVersioned` · `d134EventsDriveStats` (drift 0 vs the nightly recount) · `d134ScopesEnforced` · `d134LatencyBudgets`.

## ⛔⛔ D130 · THE STANDALONE SURVEY — one link straight to the form, no sign-up, no drafts, for people who can't try the app — 2026-11-01

## ⛔⛔ D129 · THE GUIDED TOUR — after sign-up, one guided path through every section, then two real drafts watched end to end, then the survey; analytics you can use — 2026-11-01

✅ Owner 11-01: *"we need a guided tour of the site with proper explanation, also gives us the chance to dictate outcomes and choices whilst making users understand what the site actually does and offers. so post sign up should be end to end guided tour until the survey traversing through all sections. im thinking, a sample resume and custom postings, starting at the deck scrolling at 0.5s each card and scrolling all the way to the top, then the full house showing all features in a guided manner, as to how they can get their best matches and what options they have, the filters, and setting them up, and then the atlas with informative and curated maps for the sample resume, both learn and user map. after this guided tour have them back at the deck, have them pick 2, traverse over to draft house have them watch it end to end and end up on the table. this is the only way users might be able to understand and give feedback. the survey is the most important part too. the user analytics should be usable."* **Replaces D124's flow steps (2)–(4) for trial accounts; D124's safety rule, caps, 10 picks and samples stand.**
**THE MECHANICS (one component, `GuidedTour`):** coach-marks on the REAL pages (never screenshots): a spotlight on the element, a short caption (≤ 2 sentences, plain words), **Back · Next**, a progress line (*"Step 4 of 11"*); the tour **sets the demo state** (filters, mode, the sample's map) so every user sees the same outcome, and in some steps **asks the user to do the one action** (*"Try the Sponsors filter"*) before Next unlocks; reduced motion → no auto-scroll, the cards step on Next; phone and laptop layouts; **a "Faster" toggle** (captions shorter, auto-steps quicker) because length loses people; the whole path aims at **≤ 8 minutes to the survey** (tour ≈ 4, drafts ≈ 2, survey ≈ 2) — measured (below).
**THE PATH:**
**(0) Pick a résumé** — D124's sample cards (only categories with ≥ 10 good picks) or *"Use my own"*; one line: *"We'll show you draft with this résumé."*
**(1) The deck** — the sample's **10 picks** dealt, then **auto-scrolled one card every 0.5 s all the way to the top** (the best match); captions: *"These 10 jobs were picked for this résumé from today's live postings, best match on top."* Then the top card's parts in turn: the match and why (*"15 of 26 skills"*), the level line (D106), how fresh it is (D107), the sponsorship chip (D121), **Pass · Save · Draft**.
**(2) Getting your best matches** — the filters (field, location / remote, level, sponsors visas, freshness), with one the user tries; *"draft reads every posting so you don't apply to jobs you can't get."*
**(3) Draft House, every feature** — with an **example state clearly labelled *"Example"*** (a few example branches so the tree isn't empty): the tree and the rings (Needs you · Ready for review · Working · Sent · Replied), a branch opened (the sentence, the next action, the leaves: what happened, answers, the form as filled, the résumé and *what we changed*), **the two modes** (Ask me first · Apply for me) and **Auto settings** (daily limit, run times, picks by email, which jobs, skip stale, pause after an interview) — *set up* in the step, then reset.
**(4) The Atlas** — **Your map** for the sample (the tree: coloured = has it, grey = not yet; a family opened; one skill's three facts: postings and closeness, mid → senior, its step on the route); then **Learn** (the circle; zoom to a card; *"finishing a piece unlocks skills on your map"*). For a field with no course yet, *"Learn: coming for your field"* and the map only.
**(5) Back to the deck: your turn** — *"Pick 2 jobs to send."* The user chooses 2 of the 10 (Draft on each).
**(6) Draft House, live** — the two branches run end to end while the user watches: tailoring (*what we changed*), filling the practice form step by step (D124), the consent box left to them (one press), **Sent**; captions name each step.
**(7) The Table** — the two applications; the confirmation in the Inbox; *"Replies, interviews and rejections land here."*
**(8) The survey** (below) — then *"Keep using draft with your own résumé"*.
**THE SURVEY — ✏✏ FINAL v2 11-01 (supersedes the "FINAL" block below; sketch `trial-survey.html` updated).** Owner: *"we can't switch on full access, don't offer it, just ask if they're interested or would be. how would they feel to no longer use? they never used it, it's a stupid question, we need surveys that can help our application … there are more important questions than this."* **Removed:** the "no longer use draft" question and the full-access offer. **The form rules of the block below stand** (Google-Form-like, dropdowns, labelled 5 stars, plain words, no internal names, never "real application" / "practice"). **18 questions, ≈ 2–3 minutes; required: 1, 2, 3, 7, 12, 15.**
**YOUR JOB SEARCH TODAY (the problem's size and the competition)** — **(1)** *Where are you with job hunting right now?* (Actively applying · Starting to look in the next few months · Employed, but open to the right offer · Student, looking for an internship or first job · Not looking right now) · **(2)** *What field are you in?* (prefilled from the résumé) · **(3)** *How long does it take you to find a job and send out a good application?* — *From finding the posting to pressing submit, for one application you're happy with.* (Under 15 minutes · 15–30 minutes · 30 minutes–1 hour · 1–2 hours · More than 2 hours) · **(4)** *How many applications do you send out when you're job searching?* (1–5 a week · 6–15 a week · 16–30 a week · More than 30 a week · I haven't started yet) · ✅ *(owner 11-01: "rest are okay" — v2 is FINAL with these two)* · **(5)** *What do you mainly use to find and apply for jobs today?* (LinkedIn or Indeed · Company career pages, one by one · Recruiters or referrals · University or school career portal · An AI or auto-apply tool · Something else → *"Which one?"* opens for the last two) · **(6)** *Have you ever paid for anything to help your job search?* — *For example a résumé writer, LinkedIn Premium, a course, or an application tool.* (No, never · Yes, under $20 in total · $20–$100 · More than $100) · **(7)** *What's the most frustrating part of job hunting for you?* (the six options + Something else → text).
**WHAT YOU JUST TRIED** — **(8–11)** the four 5-star questions as in the block below (job matches · applying for you · your skills map · your application tracker; *"What would make this 5 stars?"* only below 5).
**YOUR VERDICT** — **(12)** *Compared with how you apply today, draft would be…* (Much better · Somewhat better · About the same · Worse) · **(13)** *Would you let draft send applications for you?* — *draft only ever answers from your own résumé and never ticks agreements for you.* (Yes, I'd let it send on its own · Yes, after I've checked the first few · Only if I approve every one · No, I'd rather apply myself) · **(14)** *Which part would help your job search most?* (the four features · None of these) · **(15)** *Would you be interested in using draft for your job search?* (Yes, as soon as I can · Yes, when I start looking · Maybe · No → *"What would change your mind?"* on Maybe / No) · **(16)** the pay question with its explanation, as in the block below · **(17)** *What's one thing that would make draft a must-have for you?* · **(18)** *Know someone job hunting who should try this?* (optional email, one invite). **No offer of access, no call.**
**THE YC NUMBERS (Admin → Trial):** time per good application × applications a week (the problem's size, in hours) · % who already paid for job-search help and how much · what they use today (the competition) · % *much / somewhat better* than today · **trust in auto-apply** (the four answers) · % *interested, as soon as I can / when I start looking* · the pay distribution · the frustration ranking · stars per feature + the "make it 5" answers · friends invited — each by field, sample and device. **TESTS (replace the block below's):** `d129SurveyDropdownsAndStars` · `d129NoInternalNames` · `d129NoRealOrPracticeWording` · `d129NoAccessOfferNoCall` · `d129FollowUpOnlyBelowFive` · `d129RequiredSix` · `d129YcNumbersComputed`.

**THE SURVEY — ✏ FINAL 11-01, worked out with the owner (sketch `trial-survey.html`; replaces the list below).** Owner: *"the survey part is lazy, the questions are not thoughtful, the text is not readable … they don't know what the table is … wherever they could have used a dropdown, there are a bunch of labels, a simple google kinda form is sufficient … i want stars and drop down menus and thoughtful questions"* · *"we don't have time for the calls, omit this … when we ask what they are willing to pay we need to make them understand what it offers … time saved to find, research, do a resume, apply … saying real application throws some doubts on our capability to do actual applications."* **FORM:** one plain page like a Google Form — a white card per question, **dropdowns** for every single choice, **5 stars** with a label per level (*Not useful · Slightly useful · Useful · Very useful · Exactly what I need*), a progress bar, readable text (16–17 px, plain words), phone-first; **no internal names** (never *The Table*, *Draft House*, *Atlas*) — every feature described in what it does; **never the words "real application" or "practice"** in the survey. Header: *"Thanks for trying draft — about two minutes. Your honest answers decide what we build next. Nothing here is shared with employers."*
**ABOUT YOU** — **(1, required)** *Where are you with job hunting right now?* (dropdown: Actively applying · Starting to look in the next few months · Employed, but open to the right offer · Student, looking for an internship or first job · Not looking right now) · **(2, required)** *What field are you in?* (dropdown, prefilled from the résumé's category, the D127 categories in plain words) · **(3)** *Roughly how many jobs did you apply to last month?* (None · 1–10 · 11–30 · 31–100 · More than 100) · **(4)** *What's the most frustrating part of job hunting for you?* (Applying and hearing nothing back · Filling out the same application forms again and again · Rewriting my résumé for every job · Finding jobs I'm actually eligible for (visa, level, location) · Not knowing which postings are real or still open · Not knowing which skills to learn next · Something else → a short text opens).
**WHAT YOU JUST TRIED** (5 stars each, the description under the title; **"What would make this 5 stars?" opens only below 5**) — **(5)** *Your job matches* — *the 10 jobs we picked for your résumé, best match first, with why each one fits* · **(6)** *Applying for you* — *draft tailoring the résumé to each job and filling out the application while you watched* · **(7)** *Your skills map* — *the map of the skills you have, the ones close to you, and what to learn next to move up* · **(8)** *Your application tracker* — *the page that lists every job you applied to, with replies and interview invites as they come in*. (Learn is not rated in this trial.)
**YOUR VERDICT** — **(9)** *Which part would you use first?* (the four above in the same words · None of these) · **(10, required)** *How would you feel if you could no longer use draft?* (radio: Very disappointed · Somewhat disappointed · Not disappointed, it isn't that useful to me) · **(11, required)** *Would you use draft for your next job applications?* (Yes, this week · Yes, when I start looking · Maybe · No → *"What would change your mind?"* opens on Maybe / No) · **(12)** *What would feel fair to pay for draft each month?* — under it: *"Think of the time each application takes you today: finding jobs that fit, checking you're eligible and the posting is still open, researching the company, rewriting your résumé for it, and filling out the form. draft does all of that for you, for as many jobs as you want."* (I'd only use it if it were free · Under $10 · $10–$20 · $20–$40 · More than $40) · **(13)** *What's one thing that would make draft a must-have for you?* (text) · **(14)** *Want draft for your own job search?* — *"The trial stops after 2 applications. We never share them with employers."* → thank-you screen.
**THE VERDICT METRICS (Admin → Trial, the YC numbers):** % *very disappointed* (the product-fit benchmark is ≈ 40 %) · % *Yes, this week* · **full access requested** (count and %) · friends invited · the pay distribution · the frustration ranking · stars per feature with the *"make it 5 stars"* answers · each cut by field, sample and device. **TESTS:** `d129SurveyDropdownsAndStars` · `d129NoInternalNames` · `d129NoRealOrPracticeWording` · `d129FollowUpOnlyBelowFive` · `d129RequiredFour` · `d129FullAccessQueuesRequest` · `d129VerdictMetrics`.

(choose the step(s) + optional text) · would you use draft for your real search (yes / maybe / no) · what would stop you (text) · what would you pay per month (nothing · < $10 · $10–20 · $20+) · email for a 10-minute follow-up (optional).

## ⛔⛔ D128 · JOB DISCOVERY — our postings findable on search engines and job aggregators, so traffic comes to draft — 2026-11-01

✅ Owner 11-01: *"another thing to line up is regarding job discovery in search engines, i couldn't find any of our postings showing up on any search engine despite searching specifically. job discovery across platforms brings traffic. we need it."*
**P0 · MEASURE WHY FIRST (likely, unconfirmed):** are job pages public (or only inside `/app`, behind sign-in)? server-rendered (or a JavaScript shell crawlers see empty)? in `robots.txt` / a sitemap? is the domain verified in Google Search Console / Bing Webmaster Tools? Report each in NOW.
**P1 · A PUBLIC PAGE PER POSTING:** `/jobs/<company>-<title>-<id>` — **server-rendered**, no sign-in to read, with what makes draft's page worth indexing over the employer's own: the posting (attributed: *"Posted by <company> on their careers site"*, the original link), **draft's reading of it** (must-have skills, the D106 level line, D107 liveness, **D121's sponsorship signal**, salary when given), related Atlas skills, and **"Draft this job"** (sign-up → the trial or the board). **`JobPosting` structured data (JSON-LD)** per Google's job-posting guidelines (title, description, datePosted, **validThrough**, hiringOrganization, jobLocation / remote, employmentType, baseSalary when present, the apply URL); a canonical URL; **when a posting closes (D107), the page says so, drops the structured data and is removed from the sitemap the same day** (search engines penalise expired jobs). Only shown categories (D127 — held postings get no public page).
**P2 · TELL THE SEARCH ENGINES:** a jobs sitemap (split per 50k URLs, `lastmod`), linked from `robots.txt` beside the Atlas sitemap; **IndexNow** pings (Bing, Yandex and others) on publish / update / close; **Google's Indexing API** for job pages on publish / close (it is the API Google offers for job-posting pages; needs a service account added as an owner in Search Console — the owner's step). **Category and location landing pages** (*"Mechanical engineer jobs in Boston"*, *"Data analyst jobs that sponsor H-1B"*) built from the board's own data — each with a real list, no thin pages.

**P4 · IT NEVER GETS WORSE:** the gold set becomes a regression test — a change to the scorer, the extraction or the vocabulary that lowers precision, recall or ρ on the gold set fails CI (the drop shown per pair). **TESTS:** `d125GoldSetVersioned` · `d125ReviewSavesProgress` · `d125AssistIsSuggestionOnly` · `d125MetricsComputed` · `d125FixesQueueable` · `d125RegressionGate`.

employers stay in date order); Skills rows ordered by what the posting stresses; Projects likewise. **(5) variety, as a preference not a quota:** no more than two bullets on the same arc; where the candidate's material supports it, one bullet showing a stakeholder or business judgment and one showing a trade-off and its outcome. **(6) the summary rules** of L1 §SUMMARY (430–480 characters, the candidate's own title and years from the runtime inputs, two or three posting-relevant strengths, no metrics) and the no-summary rules. **(7) kept from the lean prompt:** verbatim posting keywords, filler and dash bans, bold keywords only. **Cost:** ≈ 400–600 static tokens (≈ 0.05¢ on Haiku) — worth it. **TESTS:** `p6fCraftFileLoadedByBothCalls` · `p6fNoSecondCopyOfRules` · `p6fBulletsOrderedByRelevance` (code check: within an employer, the bullet carrying the most must-have terms comes first) · `p6fNumbersKeptAndForward` · `p6fContributionVerbsWithoutSoleOwnership`.
- **P6g · THREE QUALITY ADJUSTMENTS + THE OWNER'S BLIND CHECK — owner 11-01 (*"yes"*):** **(1) the original bullets travel with the gist** and the model **rewords them first** (keeping their numbers and specifics); it writes a NEW bullet only for a must-have term the employer's gist genuinely supports; **(2) the per-employer gist is built once with the Sonnet tier** (≈ 1¢ once per résumé — everything downstream depends on it), tailoring stays Haiku; **(3) keyword density cap:** ≤ 2 posting terms bolded per bullet, no term in more than 2 bullets. **Plus a truthful way to get numbers:** when the gist is built, bullets with no number are listed on the Profile once — *"Add a real number if you have one (users, %, time saved, scale)"* — optional; added numbers become the candidate's own. **ACCEPTANCE — THE BLIND CHECK (in the live runs):** 20 résumés (the owner's + the samples × postings), today's full call vs the new lean call, **sides hidden**; the owner picks the better one per pair; recorded with ATS before / after and cost. **Pass = the new one wins or ties on ≥ 14 of 20 at ≤ 1¢.** If it loses, raise the bullet step to the Sonnet tier for that kind of posting and re-run. **TESTS:** `p6gOriginalsSentAndRewordedFirst` · `p6gGistBuiltOnceSonnet` · `p6gDensityCap` · `p6gNumbersPromptOptional` · `p6gBlindCheckRecorded`.

**✅ P7 · THE APPLY WORKER ANSWERS ROUTINE QUESTIONS WITH HAIKU — owner 11-01** (*"i am inclined towards making the auto apply call haiku to answer some basic questions based on the candidates profile and tailored resume ats blob when needed. these are jargon questions that are a formality at this volume, unless the user wants to answer them in which case they would have applied by themselves"*). ⛔ **A RECORDED DELIBERATE REVERSAL of D17** (*"only résumé generation may call a model"*) **and of D104 P2** (*"no `model` source exists for an answer"*) — enter both in `CORRECTIONS_REGISTER.md`. **What it answers:** free-text and choice questions the Profile and saved answers don't cover — *why this company, describe a project with X, how would you rate your experience with Y, what interests you about this role* — from **the Profile, the tailored résumé's ATS blob (the terms and gists of P6a) and the posting's job block**; ≤ 120 words; plain, first person, no buzzwords. **What it NEVER answers (unchanged, D100 / D104):** eligibility, work authorisation, sponsorship, citizenship, clearance, criminal history, disability / EEO, salary (from Application defaults or Needs you), consent / terms / attestation boxes, human checks; **a number** (years, team size, rating on a numeric scale) comes only from the Profile or a saved answer, never from the model. **Every model-written answer is marked** `source: model` on the Form tab (*"written by draft"*), saved as the user's answer for that question only if the user keeps it; in **SEMI** the user sees it before sending (D113's *Show me the form* stays available), in **FULL AUTO** it is sent and listed in the run summary. A setting **"Answer routine questions for me"** (on by default; off → they go to Needs you). Same lean client (P3), Haiku tier, cached per (posting, question). **Cost:** ≈ 0.1–0.2¢ per question (measure). **TESTS:** `p7AnswersOnlyRoutine` · `p7NeverEligibilityConsentSalaryHumanCheck` · `p7NumbersFromProfileOnly` · `p7SourceModelMarked` · `p7SemiShowsBeforeSend` · `p7SettingOffSendsToNeedsYou` · `p7CachedPerQuestion` · `p7CorrectionsRegistered`.

**THEN: END TO END, SEMI AND FULL AUTO (the acceptance after P6 + P7):** the owner's walk on production with his own résumé — (1) **SEMI:** a pick → Apply → P6 tailoring (the pop-up once) → the worker fills, P7 answers the routine questions → Ready for review → Approve & send → confirmation in the Inbox → The Table; (2) **FULL AUTO:** switch on (the pop-up appears here, not mid-run) → the next run picks → tailored → filled → sent → the summary lists what draft answered; plus the trial (`/try`) with a sample. Each step's cost read from the ledger; any break becomes a row.

**TARGETS:** median cost per tailored résumé **≤ 1¢**, guard pass ≥ today's, ATS lift ≥ today's, p50 latency ≤ today's. **TESTS:** `d123OneCallPerTailoring` · `d123ChangesOnlyJson` · `d123RepairOnceThenStop` · `d123HaikuDefaultSonnetFallback` · `d123CacheOnStaticBlock` · `d123BatchForScheduledOnly` · `d123ModelClientProviderNeutral` · `d123NoOtherModelCalls` · `d123CostLoggedPerResume`.

## ⛔⛔ D119 · THUMBNAILS — every resource shows what it is before you open it — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"there are links all over for books, videos etc., but no thumbnails, mere text, thumbnails take it to the next level."* **One resolver, one tile component, used by Learn (D115/D117 items), Atlas resources (D105), D114's popup and Your map's Learn next.** No model (D17).
**P1 · WHERE EACH PICTURE COMES FROM (by item kind / URL):** **video with a watch URL** (youtube.com/watch, youtu.be) → YouTube's own thumbnail for that video id + its title / channel from YouTube oEmbed · **video that is a YouTube SEARCH link** (the tracker's `yt()` helper makes many of these) → there is no single video, so **no thumbnail is invented**: a draft tile *"YouTube · search: <query>"* with a play glyph; Admin → Atlas → Learn gets **"Pin a video"** per item (paste a watch URL → the real thumbnail); the agent reports how many video items are search links vs watch links · **book** → Open Library's search API (title + author) → its cover id → the cover image, shown with *"Cover: Open Library"*; no match → a typographic book tile (title, author, the part's colour) · **article / course / guide / sandbox / practice / game** → the page's own share image (`og:image`, else `twitter:image`) fetched server-side (descriptive User-Agent, 5 s timeout, ≤ 2 MB, robots.txt honoured), else the site's icon on a tile in the item kind's colour with the domain.
**P2 · STORED, NOT HOT-LINKED:** each picture is fetched once, resized (≤ 480 px wide, WebP), stored in draft's asset store keyed by URL hash, refreshed monthly with the dead-link check (D105 P6); a failed fetch keeps the tile fallback. **Admin can hide any picture** (one press) — the takedown path. Pictures are **never** placed in documents (résumé, PDF, cover letter).
**P3 · THE TILE (one component, `ResourceTile`):** picture (16:9 video, 2:3 book, square for sites) · kind badge (Video · Book · Game …; rounded square, never a pill) · title · source · *optional* / *new* tags · its C8 state (*opened* — never *done*) · the whole tile is the link (opens in a new tab and records the D117 C8 *opened*). Grid that wraps (fluid, no fixed widths), lazy-loaded images with the title as `alt`; four themes; contrast themes add a solid outline.
**TESTS:** `d119WatchUrlThumbnail` · `d119SearchLinkNoInventedThumb` · `d119PinAVideo` · `d119OpenLibraryCover` · `d119OgImageStoredNotHotlinked` · `d119FallbackTile` · `d119AdminHide` · `d119NeverInDocuments` · `d119TileRecordsOpened` · `d119OneTileComponent`.

## ⛔⛔ D122 · ONE OBJECT, ONE COMPONENT — every page shows the same job, the same résumé, the same buttons — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"consistency of modularity across the platform. when i click on a job or resume for a specific job or a specific object, it is a single object and its instances should point towards a single object. currently one page says the job has a resume, one doesn't, one resume viewer features the editor another one doesn't. also the same with use of functions and buttons and designs we use across, like the utility draft logo buttons, and anything else."*
**THE RULE:** each object — **Posting · Application (a user's relation to a posting: status, its résumé version, form, emails) · Résumé version (base / tailored for one application) · Profile · Company · Atlas node · Learn piece** — has **ONE read path** (one server function / route) and **ONE view component** with modes (card · row · detail); **what a view can do comes from the object's own state, never from the page it sits on.** E.g. *"this job has a résumé"* = `application.resume_version_id` read through one function by the board, Draft House, The Table, the job page and the extension alike; **the résumé viewer shows the editor whenever the version is editable by this viewer** (a tailored version not yet submitted, or a base résumé), on every page.
**P1 · AUDIT FIRST (no changes):** `docs/OBJECT_MAP.md` — for each object: its read function(s), every component that renders it, every page that uses them, and **every divergence** found (two answers to "has a résumé", viewers with / without the editor, duplicated job-detail renderers …), each with file:line. `docs/UI_PRIMITIVES.md` — the shared pieces (**DepthButton** — the utility draft-logo buttons · **CompanyBubble** — the bubble standard · the status ring · the fan / card · SectionHeading · drawers · toasts · empty states · ResourceTile, D119) and **every hand-rolled copy** of one. The owner glances at both; then:
**P2 · CONSOLIDATE, worst first:** (1) the résumé's state and viewer (one `ResumeView`, the editor rule above) · (2) the job's detail (one `JobView`, every entry point — D102's "same detail everywhere" made true) · (3) buttons → DepthButton, bubbles → CompanyBubble, cards → the fan · (4) the rest of the audit's list. **No feature work rides on this lane.**
**P3 · GUARDS so it stays fixed:** a test that each object's state is read through its one function (a second query for "has a résumé" fails CI) · a lint guard: no ad-hoc styled `<button>` in `client/src` where DepthButton applies, no second bubble / card implementation · **an admin "Components" page** that renders every primitive in all four themes — the visual inventory. **TESTS:** `d122OneReadPathPerObject` · `d122ResumeStateSameEverywhere` · `d122ResumeEditorRuleFromState` · `d122OneJobView` · `d122NoAdHocButtons` · `d122OneBubbleOneCard` · `d122ComponentsPageRenders`.

## ⛔⛔ D117 · LEARN AS A CIRCLE — the course broken into pieces that each stand alone and each stay part of the whole; start anywhere, go back to understand, go forward to grow — 2026-10-31 (VISION RECORDED; design next, with the owner)

✅ Owner 10-31, on D115's tracker: *"it is a very extensive material source very rich and resourceful but feels like a one directional one one cant get a grip on. it can be tweaked to be a full circle, kinda like the movie arrival, where the circles represent completeness and that there is no beginning and end. what i mean is that the elements of this can be broken into pieces and be curated to cater its audience while it still remains a piece of the whole thing. one can start it from the beginning and go all the way, they should be able to do that, but also begin somewhere and go backwards to make sense of stuff they dont understand or forwards to progress, and it should be meaningful and seamless either way. it should be further enriched to enable exactly this, with guided directions as needed. lets start these, i want these to be a standout feature."*
**What this row fixes now (design follows in a sketch):** (0) ⭐ **D116 M8 binds this design** (owner 10-31: *"when they complete a course they can unlock these"*): every piece must say **which Atlas nodes it teaches**, and completing a piece (its required items done + its checkpoints explained) is what **unlocks** those nodes on Your map — so the piece ↔ node link is part of D117's data, not an afterthought; (1) **every step is a self-contained piece** — entered from anywhere (the Atlas, a posting's hover popup, Your map, search) and readable alone; (2) **every step knows its neighbours in BOTH directions** — *"Before this"* (what it assumes: the steps and concepts it builds on) and *"After this"* (what it opens) — so a learner can walk backwards to make sense of something or forwards to grow; (3) **the linear path from Step 1 stays** as one way round the circle, never removed; (4) **guided directions** — short routes through the pieces for a purpose (*"Make sense of Kubernetes"*, *"Backend → senior"*, *"Get ready for system design interviews"*), each a list of existing steps, so the content is curated per audience without being rewritten. ⚠ **The prerequisite links are the new data this needs** — the tracker's order gives "after" for free; "before" (what a step assumes) must be added per step. How (owner by hand, the chat assistant drafting for his review, or derived from the concept index's step pointers) is decided with the sketch. **Not built until the owner picks the design.** D115 P5 (exercises, games, practice sites) is planned inside this design.

**✏ D117 DESIGN, SKETCHED 10-31 (owner: *"d117 and also d115 p5 and the exercises and other curated materials (exercises, games, books) planned"*) — sketch `learn-circle.html` (built on his real tracker: 108 steps, 373 items, 324 checkpoints, word for word), data file `learn-d117-data.json`; PENDING his look.**
**C1 · THE PIECE (the unit; every step becomes one):** `id · title · goal · part / phase (where it sits on the whole) · items[] (with kind; optional flag) · checkpoints[] · needs[] ("Before this") · opens[] ("After this" = the inverse of needs, computed, never stored) · teaches[] (Atlas nodes — D116 M8's unlock link)`. A piece is **readable alone** and always says *"Part 4 · Distributed systems · one piece of the whole"* and *"piece 54 of 108"*. **Finished** = every non-optional item done AND every checkpoint marked *explained* (the tracker's own rule). Progress per user, server-side (D115 P3).
**C2 · WHERE THE LINKS COME FROM (measured 10-31 on the real data):** **teaches[] — DERIVED, free:** the concept index points 385 terms at the step that teaches them; **105 of 108 steps teach ≥ 1 indexed concept** → D116 M8's piece ↔ node link needs no writing (the concept nodes resolve to Atlas nodes through the thesaurus; a node a step's title names also counts). **needs[] — NOT derivable:** scanning each step's text for concepts another step teaches gives a before-link for only **28 of 108** (0.3 per step) — too thin. → **The chat assistant DRAFTED needs[] for all 108** (2–3 each, from the subject matter; e.g. *System design ← Distributed systems, DNS/HTTP/TLS, Inside a database*; *Transformers ← Neural networks, Language processing, Linear algebra*); **checked: no loops**; 32 pieces open nothing (they round off their part). **Status `drafted`, for the owner's review** in Admin → Learn (*Accept · Edit · Reject* per piece, *Accept all* after reading) — the same pattern as D105 P11's definitions; a link may point FORWARD on the path (e.g. *Computer graphics ← Linear algebra*, which comes later) — that is the circle. ## ⛔⛔ D116 · YOUR MAP — the Atlas home, built from the user's résumé: what you have, what grows you to the next level, adjacent domains, branches — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"it need not be a search only empty board, atlas can feature a profile specific board for the user based on their resume. stuff they have, stuff they can explore, like natural progression related skills kinda to advance to senior levels, or branches or adjacent domains so forth and so on."*

**ALL COMPUTED FROM DATA DRAFT ALREADY HAS — no model (D17):** the user's Profile skills (D101, from the résumé parse) · the board's per-node counts (D105 P3) · the `used_with` / `requires` edges (P9) · each posting's real level (`level_read`, D106) · the user's target role(s) from their job profile.
**THE FIVE SECTIONS (signed in; each item a node bubble — the bubble standard — opening its page; each section capped at 12 with "see all"):**
1. **You have** — the user's skills that are Atlas nodes, grouped by kind, each with *"asked for in 940 open postings"*.
2. **To reach the next level** — for the user's target role: **skills whose share of that role's postings rises from the user's level to the next** (e.g. entry/early → mid, mid → senior; share in next-level postings minus share in current-level postings, ≥ 10 points, ≥ 20 postings at each level), not on the profile, ranked by the rise. Line: *"In 61 % of senior Backend postings vs 22 % of mid"*. **This is the "natural progression to senior" — measured from the board, not opinion.**
3. **Adjacent** — `used_with` neighbours of the user's skills that are not on the profile, ranked by demand (*"Often asked with Kubernetes and Go"*).
4. **Branches** — other roles where the user already covers ≥ 40 % of the role's top 15 required skills: *"You cover 9 of 15 for Data Engineer — missing: Spark, Airflow, dbt …"*, ranked by coverage, then demand.
5. **Learn next** — the D115 steps that teach the top gaps from sections 2–4, with the user's progress on each.
**Signed out / no résumé:** the home shows search, **Learn** (D115), and **Explore by role** (the board's biggest roles, each opening its role page with its top skills) — never an empty search page. A one-line prompt: *"Upload a résumé and this page becomes your map."*
**Refresh:** on profile change and nightly after the board stats. **Thresholds are constants in one file** (10 points, 20 postings, 40 %, 12 per section) so they can be tuned from real use.
**SKETCH FIRST:** the chat assistant sketches the home (`atlas-your-map.html`) for the owner before the UI is built; the agent builds the computation and its API (`GET /api/atlas/me`) now.

**THE MAP (owner 10-31, after `atlas-map-options.html`; sketch `atlas-map-combined.html` — PENDING his look):** *"im leaning towards families map, with a hint of the older map … we should make these best things come together. and also similar map for each roles and family would be great in their respective atlas pages."* → **the Families layout with the first map's look, every position a measurement:** five family wedges (ML · Systems · Infra · Data · Backend — a node's family is a stored field, assigned once per node in the admin editor) · the user's skills on the inner ring of their family · **every other node's distance from the centre = how close it is to the user** (share of its postings that also ask for 2+ of the user's skills; dashed guide rings at 80 / 65 / 50 %) · **size = postings** (toggle: size by the rise toward senior) · **ring = have / rises toward senior for the user's role / other** · a family label shows *"you have 3 of 9"* and lights that direction. **Clicking a node shows the owner's three chosen facts:** (1) *"Prometheus is asked for in 280 open postings, and 57 % of those also ask for two or more skills you have"* (the grid's sentence) · (2) *"System design: 22 % of mid ML postings, 61 % of senior (+39 points)"* (the slope's sentence, with a small mid→senior bar) · (3) *"MLflow: step 3 of 8 on your route to senior ML Engineer; 79 % close to what you know, so it comes early"* (the climb's sentence) — plus dashed lines to the user's skills it is asked with, and **Enter the course here** (D117). **The same map on every ROLE page** (centre = the role; distance = share of that role's postings asking for the skill — core in, specialist out; signed in, rings show have / missing) **and every FAMILY page** (centre = the family; distance = share of postings asking for any skill in the family). The rest of Your map (the five sections) stays as sketched in `atlas-your-map.html`. **TESTS (when approved):** `d116MapDistanceIsCloseness` · `d116MapSizeIsPostings` · `d116ThreeFacts` · `d116RoleMapDistanceIsShare` · `d116FamilyMapDistanceIsShare` · `d116FamilyFieldStored`.

**✏ THE MAP, REVISED 10-31 (owner on `atlas-map-combined.html`):** *"love the idea but the map still looks cluttered and like a flight radar, we want it as a neural network kinda thing we can manoeuvre but is not too complicated, so having labels that would traverse us to specific points like we travelled through the neural network looks cool. but love the set up lets stick with this, just concentrate on the map."* → **the set-up stays** (families, closeness, size = postings, the ring, the three facts, Enter the course here); **the drawing becomes a layered network:** columns left → right = **You · Your skills · Very close (≥ 75 %) · Close (60–75 %) · A stretch (< 60 %)** (closeness bands), rows = the five families; edges = *asked with* (You → your skills → the skills each is asked with); edges faint until a node is chosen, then **its path back to You lights** (You → the skill of yours → it). **Manoeuvre:** drag to pan, wheel / pinch / + − to zoom, labels appear as you zoom in (always for the chosen node and its path). **Waypoints that travel:** a row of labels — *You · Your skills · Next up · Toward senior · ML · Systems · Infra · Data · Backend* — each **flies the view** to that point; **"Fly my route"** travels step by step along the route to the user's aim, the side panel following. ## ⛔⛔ D114 · ATLAS TERMS IN THE POSTINGS — a published term in a job description is a quiet link; hovering shows what it is and that it leads to learning — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"there also needs to be embeddings through out the job postings wherever these words are, for example the kubernetes word was published successfully, but needs to be earmarked as described, doesnt necessarily need to be marked or underlined but hovering needs to give a small popup to it meaning and signaling it is a learning resource link."* *("Embeddings" here = links embedded in the text — plain text matching against the Atlas and its thesaurus, no vectors, no model, D17.)*

**P1 · WHICH WORDS (server-side, per posting, cached):** a span is linked only when **(a)** it resolves through `skill_synonyms` / the Atlas `alias_of` edges to a **published** node, and **(b)** the scorer already extracted that skill for THIS posting (the posting's own skill list is the allowlist — so "go to market" never links Go, and "React to incidents" never links React). Longest match first ("machine learning engineer" before "machine learning"); whole words only; case-insensitive except the ambiguous short terms (`AMBIGUOUS_TERMS`, one- and two-letter names), which need the exact case. **Only the FIRST occurrence of each term per posting** is linked. Output: `[{start, end, slug}]` over the plain description text, returned with the posting (`GET …/postings/:id` gains `atlasSpans`); recomputed when a node is published or unpublished and nightly with the board stats. ⛔ No change to the description text itself.
**P2 · WHERE:** every place draft shows a posting's description — the board's job detail, the job page's Job tab (`/app/job/:id`), Draft House's "The job" leaf (D113 UI U4), the extension's ATS panel when it shows the description. ⛔ **Never** in documents (résumé preview, PDF, cover letter — never themed, never annotated), never on the company's own page (the extension does not rewrite third-party pages — a separate owner decision if ever wanted).
**P3 · AT REST: no mark** (the owner's call). **On hover / focus:** the cursor becomes a pointer and a faint dotted underline appears under that word only. **Keyboard:** each linked term is a real link (`<a href="/atlas/<slug>">`, in the tab order); focus opens the same popup. **Touch:** a tap opens the popup (no navigation); the popup's link navigates. ⭐ *Assistant's addition (accessibility):* **Settings → Appearance → "Show learning links"** (off by default) draws the dotted underline at rest — ✅ **kept by the owner 10-31 ("yes to all three")**.
**P4 · THE POPUP (small, ~280 px, D92 surfaces, four themes, never clipped):** the term and its kind (*tool · skill · role*) · **one or two lines of meaning** — the node's own definition, else the first sentence of its Wikipedia summary marked *"From Wikipedia"* (CC BY-SA, D105) · *"Asked for in 312 open postings"* · signed in: *"You: on your profile"* / *"Not on your profile yet"* (D101) · a book-mark glyph + **"Learn it in the Atlas →"** (the signal that this is a learning link) and, when the node has one, its first resource (*"Official docs"*). Opens after 300 ms of hover, stays while the pointer is on the word or the popup, closes on leave / Escape; one popup at a time. Data from `GET /api/atlas/peek/:slug` (name, kind, one-line meaning, count, first resource; public, cached 1 h), fetched on first hover, never preloaded for the whole posting.
**P5 · MEASURE:** count popup opens and Atlas visits from a posting (no content, no user id in the count) — the evidence of whether this is used.

**TESTS (mutation-checked):** `d114OnlyPublishedNodes` · `d114OnlyPostingsOwnSkills` (a term in the text but not in the posting's skill list is not linked) · `d114AmbiguousNeedsExactCase` ("Go" links, "go" does not) · `d114LongestMatchFirst` · `d114FirstOccurrenceOnly` · `d114TextUnchanged` · `d114NeverInDocuments` · `d114NoMarkAtRest` (unless the setting) · `d114KeyboardFocusOpens` · `d114TapOpensNotNavigates` · `d114WikipediaAttributed` · `d114PeekLazy` · `d114UnpublishRemovesSpans` · `d114FourThemes`.

**🟡 43u (10-31, night) — D114 BUILT, `6c71d79` (migration **193_atlas_link_counts**), local, NOT pushed** (so production has no popups yet — they arrive with the push). All fourteen tests in `test/d114AtlasInPostings.test.js`, **mutation-checked**: eight rules broken one at a time, each red, bytes restored (the left word edge had no test until "ArGo" was added). **Three deviations, each measured or forced:** **(1) P1(b)** — only **801 of 2,616** local postings carry `skills_json`, so a list-only rule leaves two thirds of the board unlinked: with a list the node must be on it; without one, the Atlas's own counting rule (the words in the text; the scorer's ambiguous words never) and a capitalised single-word name only in its own case ("React", never "react to incidents"). **(2) P1 output** — `[{start, end}]` offsets over the plain text do not survive `formatPosting` (the body is redrawn as blocks), so `GET /api/atlas/terms/:jobId` answers each node's FORMS and one shared pure linker (`shared/atlasLinks.js`) finds them in the text as each surface draws it; the text is unchanged (`d114TextUnchanged`). **(3) P2** — Draft House's "The job" leaf and the extension's ATS panel draw NO description text, so nothing to link there: **no `extension/` change, no zip, no version bump**.
